properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-18, Anniston City Council unanimous adoption of Resolution No. 26-R-97 (added to the agenda by amendment)
properties.duration: 12 months, effective immediately; council may shorten or extend. Planning Commission to report recommendations within six months.
properties.trigger: Planning Commission recommendation; existing zoning does not address large-scale data centers (electrical demand, water/wastewater, stormwater, noise, lighting, generators, neighborhood compatibility). City already hosts a 2 MW colocation facility (FirmFarm).

properties.duration: 180 days from the March 3, 2026 adoption/vote date, expiring August 30, 2026 (March 3 plus 180 days). WBRC and Birmingham Times both confirm the March 3, 2026 vote date and the six-month term; no separate publication-date lag was found or is needed for this calculation.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap and project pressure from large/hyperscale proposals; city cited need to review zoning, land-use policy, infrastructure readiness, environmental responsibility, neighborhood compatibility, and transparent approval procedures

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-06, Calera City Council motion approving a 6-month moratorium on data centers (5 ayes, 1 abstention), per minutes approved 2026-07-20
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Not stated in the minutes; Shelby County cities acting amid data center proposals in the county.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21, Chelsea City Council unanimous voice vote adopting Resolution 2026-07-21-1407
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Proactive; zoning ordinance does not address data centers; no credible proposal in city limits, though nearby communities have projects.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-22 (Monday), Cullman City Council unanimous adoption of Resolution No. 2026-116
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: City will examine existing zoning districts and assess potential impacts of data centers on residents' quality of life during the moratorium

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-27 (City adoption of Ordinance 1174)
properties.duration: 180-day prospective moratorium beginning on the ordinance's effective date (publication/posting date not located)
properties.trigger: Pause on new data centers, data center support facilities, and material expansions; exempts two specified parcels at 7199 and 7160 Aaron Aronov Drive and preserves vested rights and existing lawful operations

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-08 (Tuesday), Foley City Council approval of the ordinance on final reading
properties.duration: Six months, in effect upon adoption
properties.trigger: Proactive; no known proposal. Time to update zoning ordinances and technical design manuals for water, air and noise, and to evaluate megawatt thresholds with city-owned Riviera Utilities.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-16 (City Council unanimous approval of a six-month data center moratorium)
properties.duration: Six months while the Planning Commission drafts zoning rules
properties.trigger: Pause on data center development while the city drafts zoning rules; officials said the city had received no data center inquiry and acted before an application arrived

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-03, Harpersville Town Council unanimous roll-call adoption (one member absent) of Ordinance 2026-08-03-03
properties.duration: Six months from the effective date (effective immediately upon adoption); expires automatically unless extended
properties.trigger: Proactive; no developer has approached the town, but nearby Wilsonville, Westover and Childersburg have been approached. Study electrical demand, water, emergency services and noise; monthly public information sessions planned.

properties.date_enacted: Reported as approved 2026-08-10 (AL.com; AL.com map); WVTM called the Aug. 10 action a first reading with second reading on Aug. 24, and council members later referred to restrictions adopted 'in June'. An amendment exempting two pre-existing projects was adopted 3-1 on 2026-09-14.
properties.duration: 180 days from the effective date (upon publication); may be extended or rescinded
properties.trigger: Zoning does not restrict certain B2/B3/M1/M2 uses near Highways 17, 52, 58 and 95; need to study appropriate regulation while a zoning rewrite is underway.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-22, per WBRC reporting of the city council vote
properties.duration: 12 months, with the possibility of an additional six-month extension
properties.trigger: City wants to study how data center facilities could affect the community before further approvals

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-14 (Hueytown City Council unanimous roll-call adoption of Resolution 7499, per the approved July 14, 2026 minutes)
properties.duration: Not stated in the minutes; the signed Resolution 7499 text (term/expiration) was not located
properties.trigger: Proposed temporary moratorium on data center-classed facilities

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-08 (Monday night), Leeds City Council, unanimous vote.
properties.duration: One year from adoption (to approximately 2027-06-08).
properties.trigger: No active data center project underway in Leeds at time of adoption; preemptive pause to allow the city to update zoning ordinances and gather public feedback, amid a wider wave of Alabama municipalities (Birmingham, Homewood, and later Pinson) considering similar pauses.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-23 (County Commission approval of a one-year moratorium on the proposed VoltCore Bitcoin-mining data center)
properties.duration: One year, to allow study of environmental, noise, and other community effects
properties.trigger: Pause targeted at the proposed 50 MW VoltCore Bitcoin-mining facility near Union Road and the Stringer watershed near Somerville, following resident petitions (more than 450 signatures reported by the vote)

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-06 (Thursday), Pinson City Council approval at its first August meeting after a 2026-07-16 first reading
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Proactive; time to define 'hyper/mega' data centers and write zoning regulations; concerns about power, water and noise seen in western Jefferson County.

properties.date_enacted: Early August 2026: NBC 15 reports the council approved a six-month moratorium on Aug. 4, 2026; the AL.com map dataset lists 8/6/2026. The proposal introduced 2026-07-23 was for a renewable 480-day term, but the adopted measure is reported as 180 days.
properties.duration: 180 days (six months) as adopted, per NBC 15 and FOX10; the earlier draft proposed a renewable 480-day term
properties.trigger: Proposed pause on new data center permits following opposition to Edged Energy's planned Telegraph Road facility near Africatown

properties.date_enacted: Not adopted as of 2026-09-18: first reading of a proposed six-month data-center moratorium ordinance in July 2026; a vote WHNT reported as scheduled for Aug. 10 had not happened per AL.com (2026-09-18)
properties.duration: Proposed six months
properties.trigger: Severe water-capacity shortage (the water board already bars new meters); the town wants a pause in place before water access resumes.

properties.date_enacted: On or about 2026-07-07, per 1819News and Yahoo/local-TV reporting of the Town Council vote
properties.duration: Reported 18-month moratorium on data centers within town limits
properties.trigger: Pause following resident opposition to a proposed Bitcoin-mining facility near Union Road

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-06 (Monday), Springville City Council
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Proactive, following community concern that Commerce Park development might be a data center (county said no); gives the planning and zoning commission time to draft regulations.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-08 (Tuesday), Tarrant City Council approval of Ordinance No. 1177 (first reading had been scheduled for the preceding Tuesday meeting per ABC 33/40)
properties.duration: 12 months (one year)
properties.trigger: Proactive; no data center developer had approached the city. City wants to study electrical capacity, water, transportation and public-safety impacts and train its planning commission before setting local standards.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-18 (Tuesday), Westover City Council unanimous vote on the moratorium ordinance (tabled at the previous meeting)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Resident opposition to a proposed data center on roughly 450 acres along U.S. Highway 280 and Cheshire Drive after the city's MOU with the developer fell through; time to study zoning and impacts.

properties.duration: Ordinance No. 26-20 proposes a temporary two-year moratorium; introduced on the consent agenda at the September 10, 2026 regular council meeting, which set a public hearing and action vote for October 8, 2026. No adoption vote had occurred as of 2026-09-23. A separate, differently-worded ordinance to block data center construction failed 4-2 at the August 13, 2026 council meeting; Ordinance 26-20 is a distinct, later measure.
properties.trigger: specific_project

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-11 (Board of Supervisors adopted an addendum-item resolution at its regular meeting, 3-2 vote)
properties.duration: 120 days from adoption (2026-08-11 to approximately 2026-12-09), to give county staff time to finalize a zoning code text amendment establishing data-center-specific regulations; Supervisor Heinz's floor amendment provided the moratorium could return to the board for possible extension before the 120-day limit.
properties.trigger: Pima County Development Services was already drafting a data-center zoning code text amendment (process initiated by a September 2025 BOS vote) when a second, undisclosed data-center project ('Project Gravel,' an 8-building, 160-acre facility near Sahuarita) surfaced via a public-records request; the moratorium bars new data center permit applications while the code amendment is finalized, and (as amended) applies to facilities that have not yet submitted a permit application, so it does not affect the previously permitted 'Project Blue' facility.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-16 (Carroll County Quorum Court unanimous adoption of Emergency Ordinance 2026-17)
properties.duration: Immediate 12-month moratorium from adoption
properties.trigger: Immediate pause on high-impact industrial and high-intensity digital infrastructure facilities (reported by contemporary coverage to include data centers, artificial intelligence computing facilities, and cryptocurrency mining facilities) in unincorporated Carroll County while the county develops a permitting and public-notice framework

properties.duration: One year or until specific land-use standards were developed, whichever occurred first
properties.trigger: Green Digital conditional-use application; Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023; zoning code did not list data centers or crypto mining facilities; concerns over electricity use, greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, e-waste, noise, and local impacts

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-10 (Independence County Quorum Court unanimous adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-21 at its regular August meeting, reported the next day as a Monday-night vote)
properties.duration: Five-year moratorium on construction of commercial data centers, effective immediately under an emergency clause; runs through Aug. 31, 2031
properties.trigger: Preemptive pause adopted with no data center project currently proposed in the county; Justices of the Peace cited the heavy water and electricity consumption of commercial data centers, lack of transparency in land acquisition, and a recent wind-turbine development dispute (a company holding turbine contracts predating the county's 2025 wind moratorium) as reasons to act before any project arrives.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-17 (Madison County Quorum Court, 8-0 vote, regular meeting)
properties.duration: Three-year moratorium on data centers, digital asset (cryptocurrency) mining businesses, and other large-scale computer/server operations; effective immediately under an emergency clause; runs through Aug. 31, 2029
properties.trigger: Preemptive pause adopted with no known data center project in development; two public hearings preceded the vote; the county wants time to study data centers and develop regulations addressing their potential costs and benefits

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-16 (City Council amended a proposed 18-month moratorium to six months by a 6-2 vote, then adopted the amended ordinance by another 6-2 vote)
properties.duration: Six-month moratorium as amended and adopted; originally proposed as an 18-month moratorium in a June 16, 2026 councilmember proposal
properties.trigger: Pause on acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for data center development, construction, or siting within city limits; officials said no active data center proposal was known

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-30 (Union County Quorum Court unanimous adoption of Ordinance 1795 at an emergency meeting); reported to run 2026-07-10 through 2027-07-09
properties.duration: One-year moratorium, reported to run from 2026-07-10 through 2027-07-09
properties.trigger: Pause on new data center development in Union County following resident concerns about electricity, water, transparency, and use of public resources

properties.date_enacted: 2026-03-04, Baldwin Park City Council adoption of an urgency ordinance establishing a 45-day moratorium; extended following a 2026-04-15 public hearing
properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-03-04; extended following an April 15, 2026 public hearing under Gov. Code section 65858, bringing the total pause to approximately one year ('yearlong ban') per regional reporting.
properties.trigger: Regional San Gabriel Valley wave of data center moratoria/bans (Monterey Park, El Monte, Montebello); city seeking time to study impacts and develop zoning standards for data center uses before any application is filed.

properties.duration: The originally proposed five-year (1,825-day) interim urgency moratorium (introduced 2026-05-12) was never brought back for a formal adoption vote. Instead, the City Council pivoted to pursuing a permanent prohibition: on 2026-07-14 the Council voted 3-2 (Chavez and Amezcua dissenting) to advance a resolution/ordinance permanently prohibiting the establishment and operation of data centers within city limits, directing staff to publish the full ordinance text and schedule a public hearing. As of a September 2026 public statement by Mayor Michael Luellen, staff had still not brought the drafted permanent ban back to the Council for a final vote.
properties.trigger: Proposed pause on new large-scale data center development pending a formal hearing process

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-04 (Coachella City Council special meeting approved an interim urgency moratorium on data centers, per NBC Palm Springs and kvcrnews.org reporting); extended on or about 2026-07-09 while the city drafts a permanent ban
properties.duration: Consistent with the Gov. Code section 65858 interim urgency ordinance pattern already documented elsewhere in this inventory (initial up to 45 days, extendable to a 2-year maximum by 4/5 vote): reported as an initial temporary/urgency moratorium adopted 2026-06-04, then extended around 2026-07-09 ('Coachella Extends Temporary Ban On Data Center Developments,' Patch) as the council moves toward a permanent ban. Exact day counts and vote margins were not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
properties.trigger: Public backlash and protests over a large proposed data center project and a power agreement with developer 'Stronghold'; council terminated the specific project and moved toward a permanent ban

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-16 (City Council adoption of a 45-day interim urgency moratorium); extended by 22 months and 15 days via unanimous City Council vote on 2026-07-07
properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-06-16; extended 22 months and 15 days from 2026-07-07, bringing the maximum total pause to the Gov. Code section 65858 two-year cap.
properties.trigger: Pause on licenses, permits, entitlements, and land-use approvals for data centers and similar high-intensity computing uses while the city studies whether, where, and under what standards such uses should be allowed; no specific data center application was reported pending

properties.date_enacted: 2026-03-18 (Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 3063, adopted by a 7-0 vote at a Concurrent Special Meeting, per published City Council minutes); extended by Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 3065, adopted by a 7-0 vote at the Regular Meeting of 2026-04-22 following a public hearing and receipt of the Gov. Code section 65858(d) report, per published minutes
properties.duration: Initial 45 days (Ord. 3063, term would have run through approximately 2026-05-02); extended 10 months and 15 days by Ord. 3065, adopted 2026-04-22. Under Gov. Code section 65858(a), the initial ordinance plus this first extension together cannot exceed one year from initial adoption, placing the current expiration at approximately 2027-04-13/14 (45 days + 10 months 15 days = 12 months from 2026-03-18). The exact date is not stated verbatim in the minutes reviewed and is calculated from the statutory ceiling, not quoted from a source.
properties.trigger: City Council study of data center development and community impacts within El Monte

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-03 (City Council unanimous adoption of Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 834, per meeting summary and a contemporaneous Coachella staff report survey of nearby municipal actions)
properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-06-03 (Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 834). Contrary to the prior 'expired' classification, the City Council held a public hearing 2026-07-15 and unanimously (5-0) adopted Urgency Ordinance No. 835, extending Ordinance No. 834 for up to 10 months and 15 days under Gov. Code section 65858, so that -- as multiple sources independently confirm -- the City of Imperial's pause on data centers, high-performance computing facilities, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) runs through approximately May 2027. This remains a distinct instrument and jurisdiction from the Imperial County Board of Supervisors' moratorium (ca-imperial-county-2026, since rescinded by court order), which covers unincorporated county land, not the City of Imperial.
properties.trigger: Pause on approvals for data centers, battery energy storage systems, and similar utility-intensive industrial/technology uses while the city studies zoning and development standards

properties.duration: Extended to a one-year moratorium on 2026-07-14; reported to run into June 2027 while the County's advisory committee develops recommendations.
properties.trigger: Months of public opposition to a large proposed data center complex projected to consume about 750,000 gallons of water daily and more electricity than the entire county used in 2024

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-03 (City Council unanimous adoption of Urgency Ordinance No. 1838); extended by a further City Council vote on 2026-07-15
properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-06-03 (Urgency Ordinance No. 1838); extended 90 days by unanimous City Council vote on 2026-07-15, keeping the pause in force through 2026-10-16 while staff drafts a permanent ban ordinance for Planning Commission and Council consideration.
properties.trigger: Pause on establishment, expansion, or intensification of data center uses to allow review of regulations and consideration of a longer moratorium or permanent prohibition; city reported no active data center applications

properties.date_enacted: Draft Urgency Ordinance 819 was scheduled for a City Council public hearing and possible four-fifths adoption vote on 2026-05-27; whether it was adopted that day is unconfirmed
properties.duration: Draft ordinance proposed a 45-day moratorium on processing, approving, or accepting new data center applications and on converting existing facilities into data centers
properties.trigger: Proposed pause on new and converted data center applications

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-17, effective date of a memorandum signed by Amy Bodek, Director of the Department of Regional Planning, implementing Board of Supervisors direction from an April 14, 2026 motion by Supervisor Hilda Solis
properties.duration: Interim administrative prohibition on processing/approving large-scale (hyperscale) AI data centers in unincorporated county zones, in effect until the Board of Supervisors adopts a permanent zoning ordinance. A motion to formally initiate that ordinance was scheduled for a Community Services Cluster Agenda Review on 2026-09-23, with a Board of Supervisors hearing expected around 2026-10-06.
properties.trigger: San Gabriel Valley community concerns over health, environmental, water, and electricity impacts of hyperscale AI data centers (following the Monterey Park/SDCF controversy and other regional moratoria); Board of Supervisors motion directing a zoning study; noise, air-quality, and utility-rate concerns cited by county Public Health and Public Works directors.

properties.duration: 45 days; statutory extensions available
properties.trigger: Regional data center proposals, including Monterey Park's 1977 Saturn Street site about one-half mile away, and concerns over electricity, water, backup generators, noise, infrastructure, land-use compatibility, and environmental impacts

properties.duration: Initial 45 days; extended 10 months and 15 days; expires 2027-01-21 unless changed
properties.trigger: 1977 Saturn Street data center proposal and broader concern over energy use, noise, air quality, aesthetics, property values, neighborhood quality of life, CEQA review, and whether permanent regulations or a citywide ban are needed

properties.duration: 45 days from 2026-04-14, extended 10 months and 15 days by a second urgency ordinance adopted 2026-05-12 (5-0 vote); the combined term runs to the Gov. Code 65858(a) one-year statutory ceiling, approximately 2027-04-13/14.
properties.trigger: Bridgehead Industrial Project public testimony and removal of data centers from that project; Oakley Municipal Code did not define or regulate data center land uses

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-26, Palm Springs City Council unanimous adoption of an urgency ordinance (item brought forward by Councilmember Grace Garner)
properties.duration: 45 days from adoption, effective immediately as an urgency ordinance; council discussed the possibility of extending for up to two years, consistent with the Gov. Code section 65858 pattern used elsewhere in the Coachella Valley.
properties.trigger: Regional wave of Coachella Valley moratoria/bans (Coachella, Desert Hot Springs, Indio); city's zoning/municipal code does not currently define or regulate data center uses; concerns over water, electricity, infrastructure, and land impacts of large-scale facilities.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-16, Patterson City Council adoption of an initial 45-day moratorium; extended by unanimous (4-0) vote on 2026-08-18
properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-07-16; extended by a 4-0 City Council vote on 2026-08-18 through 2027-07-15. State law caps the total moratorium period at two years.
properties.trigger: Study of potential effects of data center development on public utilities (water, energy infrastructure), air quality, and noise levels in nearby communities; city in early stages of determining how to regulate data centers long-term.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-15, Richmond City Council adoption of an urgency ordinance (regular meeting)
properties.duration: 45 days from the date of adoption, effective immediately as an urgency ordinance (four-fifths vote), extendable under Gov. Code section 65858.
properties.trigger: City's municipal code does not specifically define or regulate data centers; council directed staff in April 2026 to return with a proposed moratorium; concerns over electricity/water use, noise, air quality, and the city's limited industrial land.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners unanimously adopted Resolution 2026-47 on 2026-06-16.
properties.duration: Six-month data center moratorium barring pre-submittal activity and the acceptance or processing of planning, building, engineering, and other development applications for data center facilities through December 15, 2026, unless terminated or extended.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-02, Commissioners adoption
properties.duration: Six months, from June 2, 2026 through the close of business on December 2, 2026, per the county's own draft resolution attached to the June 2, 2026 Business Meeting agenda.

properties.date_enacted: City Council voted 9-0 to adopt Ordinance 2313 on second and final reading, 2026-07-07.
properties.duration: Stops acceptance, pre-submittal activity, and processing for new or expanded data center facilities and other large energy users with projected loads of at least 10 MW. The pause lasts 18 months from its effective date, or until relevant municipal definitions and standards are adopted, whichever occurs first; council retained authority to extend it. Effective seven days after publication following final passage.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Trustees voted 6-0 to adopt Emergency Ordinance 2026-13 on 2026-06-09, following a 2026-05-20 Planning and Zoning Commission introductory discussion and 2026-05-12 Board of Trustees support for staff work.
properties.duration: Pauses acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for principal-use data centers through December 9, 2026, unless shortened or extended. Accessory computer/server equipment serving another lawful principal use is excluded.
properties.trigger: Followed Planning and Zoning Commission discussion of treating data centers as a distinct land use.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Trustees adopted at its August 20, 2026 regular meeting on a 6-1 vote (Mayor Pro Tem Atkinson dissenting); the ordinance was introduced as 'Ordinance 2026-XX' and initially recorded as Ordinance 2026-06, but the Board's Record of Proceedings was formally amended on 09/17/2026 (after Board approval on 09/03/2026) to correct the ordinance numbering to Ordinance 2026-07.
properties.duration: Emergency ordinance imposing a temporary moratorium on data center facility applications and pre-submittal activity in all zoning designations within the Town, continuing until the earliest of February 20, 2027 or adoption of permanent data-center definitions/standards into the Cedaredge Municipal Code.
properties.trigger: Board referral by Trustee Hoffbauer under Trustee Comments on 8/6/2026, citing lack of adequate local standards for data center facilities; expedited as an emergency ordinance given potential impacts on Town water supply and availability.

properties.duration: Draft ordinance would impose a six-month moratorium on approving data center development plans and zoning applications, because the City's land development code does not address the 'unique characteristics of data center facilities.' Staff recommendation was to pass the six-month ban as written; if adopted, the city would not approve data center development plans until approximately March 2027, extendable by further council vote.
properties.trigger: City staff cited significant potential impacts of data centers on city infrastructure (power and water supply), neighborhood character, and surrounding land use, given the land development code's silence on data-center-specific standards.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners adopted Resolution R-18 on 2026-07-07.
properties.duration: Temporary moratorium on data center facility applications in unincorporated Delta County, covering pre-submittal activity and planning, building, engineering, and other development applications. Scheduled to expire January 7, 2027, or when the county adopts permanent regulations, whichever occurs first.
properties.trigger: County review will consider land-use compatibility, water and energy demand, infrastructure, noise, environmental effects, emergency response, and economic development.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-18 (City Council final passage of Council Bill 26-0431 at second reading/public hearing, unanimous); signed by the Mayor 2026-05-20; effective 2026-05-21
properties.duration: One year from the effective date (2026-05-21, i.e. nominally through 2027-05-21), or upon adoption of amendments to the Denver Revised Municipal Code and a text amendment to the Denver Zoning Code addressing data centers, per Section 5 of the ordinance as filed and passed without amendment to that section: 'This moratorium shall expire the earlier of: (a) One year from the effective date of this ordinance; or (b) The effective date of any amendments to the Denver Revised Municipal Code regarding data centers and any text amendment to the Denver Zoning Code regarding data centers, whichever occurs later.' (The 'earlier of ... whichever occurs later' phrasing is the ordinance's own internal drafting inconsistency, quoted verbatim.)
properties.trigger: No data-center-specific zoning regulations; concerns about water, energy, ratepayer cost shifting, noise, air quality, siting, and impacts on vulnerable communities.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners approved at its June 9, 2026 meeting in Hot Sulphur Springs.
properties.duration: Moratorium on construction of data centers under the county's state-delegated 1041 authority, deliberately aligned to expire on the same date as the county's existing two-year moratorium on commercial/utility-scale solar and wind facilities over 25 kW (adopted June 24, 2025).
properties.trigger: Commissioners determined data centers fall under the same 1041 category as solar/wind facilities and should be reviewed together; no existing data center regulations in the county.

properties.date_enacted: Town Council unanimously approved Ordinance 26-13 on second/final reading (6-0) on 2026-07-01, following a 5-1 first reading on 2026-06-17.
properties.duration: Temporary moratorium on new data center facility applications while the town evaluates land-use and infrastructure regulations. Precise duration, effective date, and exceptions were not located in reviewed sources.

Ten-month moratorium adopted at a May 19, 2026 public hearing on new applications for development of, or rezoning to allow, data centers in unincorporated Jefferson County; excludes land already zoned for data centers via a Planned Development at least 1,500 feet from any dwelling. Runs through approximately March 19, 2027.
properties.trigger: Commissioners cited the need to evaluate how data centers interact with the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI), the county's water supply, environment, and community health, while weighing potential job growth against community impact (per the county's official news release).

properties.date_enacted: Town Council passed Ordinance 2026-295 on a 5-1 vote at its Monday, July 20, 2026 meeting (Mayor Duncan, Mayor Pro Tem Young, and Councilmembers Berg, Morris, and Menzies voting aye; Councilmember Bashford opposed; Councilmember Molinar absent).
properties.duration: 12-month moratorium (or until Johnstown adopts data-center definitions, standards, regulations, and conditions into its Land Use Development Code, whichever is first) on accepting applications or engaging in pre-submittal activities for data-center facilities, including planning applications, building permits, and engineering permits.
properties.trigger: Town officials cited the lack of comprehensive zoning, land-use, or water-management regulations addressing data centers' potential burden on the town's long-term energy, water, and fiber resources; no data center project has been proposed in Johnstown.

properties.duration: Initial 30 days from 2026-01-27 (Resolution, Reception No. 20260005307); extended six months to 2026-08-25 by a resolution signed 2026-04-07 (Reception No. 20260016505), following a 2026-02-09 public hearing; extended a second time, six more months, to 2026-02-25 (2027), by a resolution signed 2026-07-13 (Reception No. 20260034886), following a 2026-07-13 public hearing.
properties.trigger: Larimer County Land Use Code had no definitions or regulations for data center uses; county cited water consumption, power usage, noise, aesthetics, heat effects, and suitable zoning.

properties.date_enacted: Town Board voted 6-1 on July 21, 2026 to approve an ordinance introduced by Mayor Jamie Jeffery.
properties.duration: Five-year pause on the Town's acceptance and review of applications for new or expanded data center facilities -- reported as the longest active data-center moratorium in Colorado.
properties.trigger: Preemptive action; no data center has been proposed in Lochbuie, but a large data center (Cielo Hudson Data Center, ~500 acres/750 MW) is planned in neighboring Hudson. Over 400 residents petitioned via an Action Network campaign organized by the nonprofit 'With Many Hands,' citing water and electricity concerns amid statewide drought.

properties.duration: 180 days as adopted; replaced by Resolution 2026-5 (effective 2026-02-17) before the full term elapsed
properties.trigger: County needed time to draft regulations before accepting or processing applications for data center, battery, solar, and wind facilities; meeting records cited grid, infrastructure, agricultural land, and land use compatibility concerns.

properties.date_enacted: City Council voted 7-2 on September 15, 2026 to adopt the suspension, after amending the staff-proposed 9-month term to 12 months on a 5-4 vote (Councilor Laura Light-Kovacs' motion).
properties.duration: 12-month suspension on the City's acceptance, processing, approval, permitting, rezoning, and site plan review of new land use applications for data centers with an electrical demand of 10 MW or more or that use industrial-scale cooling infrastructure; ends upon adoption of comprehensive Unified Development Code data-center regulations or 12 months from the effective date, whichever is first.
properties.trigger: No pending applications, but staff and council cited the lack of statewide regulation after SB26-102 and HB26-1030 were both postponed indefinitely, and the need for the City to coordinate with the Platte River Power Authority on grid impacts and study water/cooling tradeoffs.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Trustees approved on a 4-2 vote (Trustees Hagan and Crane dissenting) at its August 31, 2026 meeting.
properties.duration: 12-month moratorium preventing data centers from applying to develop in Mead; does not permanently prohibit data centers, and can end sooner than 12 months if staff has adequate information to develop regulations.
properties.trigger: Town Attorney Marcus McAskin cited increasing interest in Front Range data center development (e.g., the proposed Global AI facility in Windsor) and substantial potential demands on electrical power, utility infrastructure, and water supply.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Trustees introduced/discussed at its May 27, 2026 regular meeting; the Town's own Municode ordinance index records final adoption as Ordinance No. 2026-839 on 7/30/2026.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on accepting/processing applications for data center uses, to give town staff time to research and develop land use regulations.
properties.trigger: Not specified in the sources reviewed beyond the general statewide pattern of pausing applications pending land use regulation development.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners adopted Resolution Number 23-2026, effective July 1, 2026.
properties.duration: Six-month moratorium (the statutory maximum a Colorado county may impose by resolution without a public hearing under C.R.S. 30-28-121) on acceptance/processing of data center facility applications in unincorporated Montrose County, from the effective date or until data-center standards are adopted into the Zoning Regulations, whichever is first.
properties.trigger: The county's Zoning Resolution does not currently contain specific regulations, standards, or definitions addressing data center facilities' impacts on electrical power, water supply, telecommunications, and transportation infrastructure.

properties.date_enacted: Town Council voted 6-0 to adopt Ordinance 18-2026 on 2026-07-20.
properties.duration: Six-month moratorium on permit and land-development applications that include a data center as a principal or accessory use.
properties.trigger: No data center proposal was pending; staff planned to address data centers in a broader rewrite of the land-development code.

properties.date_enacted: Town Board passed by unanimous vote at the August 11, 2026 regular board meeting; resolution drafted by Interim Town Administrator Greg Sund.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium tied to Resolution 15-26, refusing data center applications until August 11, 2027; also directs staff to draft a data-center-specific ordinance.
properties.trigger: Followed neighboring Delta County's data-center moratorium; Mayor Pro Tem Anne Lee Foster called the pause 'very prudent,' and trustees discussed coordinating with the county on water-policy impacts.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners adopted at its meeting on Tuesday, May 5, 2026.
properties.duration: Emergency temporary moratorium on data center project applications (acceptance, processing, or approval) for six months, to give the County time to develop and amend the Saguache County Land Use Code, Standards, and 1041 Regulations addressing data center projects.
properties.trigger: San Luis Valley Rural Electric Cooperative (SLVREC) CEO Eric Eriksen told commissioners at an April 21, 2026 meeting that the co-op had received three inquiries for 'rural data center' projects in the Valley; commissioners cited the need for 'immediate preservation and protection of the public health, safety, and welfare.'

properties.date_enacted: The Town Board of the Town of South Fork introduced and passed Emergency Ordinance No. 2026-03 on June 18, 2026, per the archived legal notice published in the Valley Courier's July 1, 2026 edition. The notice's own adoption clause misstates the enacting body as 'Town of Center,' which is judged to be a drafting/scrivener error: every other part of the notice -- its heading ('TOWN OF SOUTH FORK'), all WHEREAS recitals, and the operative sections (which reference amending 'the South Fork Revised Municipal Code' and 'the South Fork Zoning Code') -- identifies the Town of South Fork, and the neighboring Town of Center's own published board-meeting calendar shows no meeting on June 18, 2026 at all.
properties.duration: One-year pause on permit and site-development applications for new primary-use data centers while the town considers code amendments and community engagement.

properties.date_enacted: City Council adopted Ordinance 1525 on 2026-07-16, following a first reading on 2026-06-18.
properties.duration: Pauses submission, acceptance, processing, review, hearings, approval, and siting of new or expanded data centers while the city develops definitions and land-use, water, and wastewater rules. City Council passed Ordinance No. 1525 (Series 2026) on second/final reading July 16, 2026 as an 18-month moratorium: The Gazette's July 17, 2026 report of that meeting states 'The 18-month moratorium halts data centers' and quotes Councilmember Seth Bryant explaining why council chose 18 rather than 12 months. The city's posted first-reading document (posted June 19, 2026, before the amendment) still shows the pre-amendment 12-month figure and blank termination-date placeholders; a signed second-reading ordinance with the filled-in date was not located, but the 18-month figure is independently corroborated by Colorado Newsline and the Denver Gazette.
properties.trigger: No data center proposal was pending at the time of adoption; described as a proactive measure.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23. Application #26-25 (a text amendment to Cromwell Zoning Regulations Section 4.2.E. to impose a 12-month moratorium on data centers) was introduced by Planning and Zoning Commission Chair Kelly; on 2026-08-18 the Commission voted 5-1 (Commissioner Michael Cannata dissenting) only to accept the application and schedule it for a public hearing at a Special Meeting on 2026-09-24 -- one day after this research date.
properties.duration: Proposed 12 months
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap: the town's zoning regulations have no definition or standards for a data center use; the moratorium proposal was introduced to pause any data center application while regulations are developed alongside a broader, already-contracted zoning-regulations rewrite (consultant IMEG). Commissioner Cannata opposed the moratorium, citing an unnamed prospective applicant who has worked with the town for nine months and already secured a property option.

properties.date_enacted: 2022-06-14 (Groton PZC adoption, 5-0 vote); effective 2022-07-15, per the adopted motion text in the June 14, 2022 PZC meeting minutes: "This text amendment shall become effective July 15, 2022."
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Local proposals for large data centers, uncertainty about how data centers differed from telecommunications facilities, and resident concerns about noise, stormwater, generator use, energy use, and environmental impacts

properties.date_enacted: The identical moratorium text (prepared by the Town Planner and dated 2026-03-23) was re-filed by the Commission under its 'regulations' folder -- rather than the earlier 'generals'/draft-agenda-attachment folder it occupied as of the April 15, 2026 meeting -- under the title 'Public Hearing Two Year Moratorium on Battery Storage Facilities and Data Centers,' with a document date of 2026-05-20. Secondary reporting describes a public hearing held on a Tuesday and Commission approval the same week, consistent with adoption around 2026-05-19/20. Neither the exact adoption-vote date nor the Connecticut-statute-required newspaper publication date (which triggers legal effectiveness) was found in any source I could access.
properties.duration: 12 months from effective date of adoption
properties.trigger: Need to evaluate land use, environmental, infrastructure, fire safety, emergency response, groundwater, traffic, noise, visual, electrical infrastructure, and water-use impacts

properties.date_enacted: Introduced 2026-07-06 as a communication by Board of Alders Majority Leader Richard Furlow (item LM-2026-0285). The Legislation Committee held a public hearing and gave a Favorable Report on 2026-08-04 (per the item's official Legistar history). The item was on the full Board of Alders' agenda for its 2026-09-08 meeting (a Tuesday, since the Board's usual Monday date fell on Labor Day). Yale Daily News reported the Board voted unanimously that Tuesday to adopt the 12-month moratorium; this is treated as the adoption date, though it could not be independently corroborated with a second source (see notes on residual uncertainty).
properties.duration: 12 months from adoption (ordinance text: 'A TEMPORARY TWELVE (12) MONTH MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT WITHIN THE CITY OF NEW HAVEN'), per the official ordinance language on file with the City/Town Clerk (Legistar file LM-2026-0285).
properties.trigger: Proactive/regulatory-gap: the city has no zoning framework for data centers and wants to develop one before any project is proposed, drawing on approaches used by Groton, Morris, and West Haven, Connecticut.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-09, Trumbull Town Council, unanimous voice vote at a public hearing/regular meeting
properties.duration: 2 years, effective immediately upon adoption
properties.trigger: specific_project concerns: 365 Data Centers (Norwalk) and Aphorio Carter (a data center division of private equity firm Carter Funds) announced in May 2026 plans for a 200 MW pipeline of AI-ready data centers, naming Trumbull's decades-old former Nasdaq data center at 80 Merritt Blvd. as a likely site for modernization into a 'high density, AI-ready' facility; a resident petition and advocacy group (Trumbull AI Data Center Watch) pushed for a moratorium and had sought (unsuccessfully) to have it cover the 80 Merritt Blvd. project itself.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-08, per City Council meeting minutes
properties.duration: 1 year
properties.trigger: Not detailed beyond the mayor's request in captured minutes

properties.duration: 18 months from the ordinance's effective date, as drafted; the Council may extend by ordinance upon findings that additional study remains necessary. Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23.
properties.trigger: Multiple inquiries about 'Large Energy Use Facilities' (data centers meeting defined MW/load thresholds); city wants time to study electrical capacity, ratepayer cost allocation, infrastructure, land use, environmental standards, and economic impact before adopting permanent regulations

properties.date_enacted: Approved by the Board of County Commissioners 2026-07-07 (reported 2026-07-08).
properties.duration: Six-month moratorium on data centers requiring 5 MW of power or more in unincorporated Bay County, while staff reviews and updates land development regulations; may be extended another six months if permanent rules are not ready.
properties.trigger: Months of public discussion and comment on proposed AI data centers in unincorporated Bay County.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-05-26 by the Board of County Commissioners at a public hearing, 5-0 vote; staff had been directed on 2026-05-12 to prepare the ordinance for that meeting.
properties.duration: In effect for 12 months from its effective date or until related county regulations take effect, whichever occurs first.
properties.trigger: County-initiated pause pending development of local data-center regulations; more than 40 public speakers attended the May 26 hearing.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-06-23 by the Board of County Commissioners, 4-1 vote, following a first hearing 2026-06-09.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium in unincorporated Clay County.
properties.trigger: More than an hour of public testimony at the final hearing.

properties.date_enacted: Commissioners approved the moratorium unanimously (4-0, one commissioner recused) 2026-07-28 (Tuesday).
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on new data-center applications in DeSoto County; explicitly does not apply to rezoning applications already pending for DCIP Group's 800-plus-acre data-center project (which can continue to move forward).
properties.trigger: Intense public opposition to DCIP Group's proposed data-center campus (initially a 34-acre rezoning at a decommissioned power plant, since expanded with an 800-plus-acre rezoning request and stated intent to build on up to 1,300 acres).

properties.date_enacted: Adopted on second reading by the Board of County Commissioners 2026-08-03 (Monday), unanimous.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on new data center development in unincorporated Flagler County while the county researches the industry and develops zoning/land development regulations. Amended before final passage to remove the 'large-scale'/'large load customer facility' qualifiers so the pause applies to all data centers, not only large ones.
properties.trigger: Months of discussion about the rapid growth of the data-center industry and resident concerns about impacts on electrical infrastructure, water, noise, and land use.

properties.date_enacted: Commissioners voted unanimously to approve the moratorium 2026-07-15 (Wednesday morning), after directing staff in June to prepare it.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on large-scale AI data center proposals, while commissioners consider a permanent ban.
properties.trigger: Precautionary; more than one commissioner stated an eventual goal of a permanent ban.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-06-23 at second public hearing (first hearing 2026-06-02); Florida Department of State acknowledged filing 2026-06-24.
properties.duration: 365-day moratorium on development orders and permits for data centers in unincorporated Hernando County, subject to exemptions and prospective-application provisions; can end early if permanent regulations take effect, and can be extended once for no more than 120 days.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously to adopt the ordinance 2026-09-09 (Tuesday).
properties.duration: 90-day pause on accepting any applications for large-scale data centers in unincorporated Lake County, to give commissioners time to create new zoning and development regulations (including a possible conditional-use-permit requirement).
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap; county wants a conditional-use-permit process so a data center is not a guaranteed right.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-03, City Commission adopted Ordinance No. 26-018 by a 4-3 vote.
properties.duration: One year from 2026-08-03, unless amended or repealed sooner. Covers new data centers and large-load customers with anticipated peak demand of 50 MW or more while the City reviews its planning and land-development rules.
properties.trigger: Followed community opposition to Project Swan, a proposed approximately 600,000-square-foot data center.

properties.date_enacted: Commissioners directed staff in July 2026 to pursue an ordinance; the proposed ordinance passed its first of two required public hearings unanimously 2026-09-15. The second and final public hearing/vote is scheduled for 2026-10-13 and had not occurred as of this research date.
properties.duration: Proposed 18-month moratorium on large-load customer facilities, including large-scale data centers, in unincorporated Leon County, to give staff time to study impacts on electricity/water supplies, utility rates, the environment, and surrounding communities and to develop regulations; staff plans to report findings by September 2027.
properties.trigger: Proposal originated with Commission Chairman Christian Caban after SB 484 took effect 2026-07-01; county code and the Tallahassee-Leon County 2050 Comprehensive Plan lack provisions addressing large-load customers/data centers.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-06-23 by City Commission.
properties.duration: Interim pause on accepting, processing, reviewing, or acting on data-center applications, lasting until the earlier of final action on a separate proposed one-year moratorium ordinance or sixty days after this resolution's adoption (on or about 2026-08-22).
properties.trigger: Adopted while a separate one-year moratorium ordinance (staff directed to draft it on 2026-06-09) proceeded through the adoption process; this resolution is a distinct interim instrument from that still-pending ordinance.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously 2026-07-22.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on construction and permitting of large-scale data centers while the county develops possible regulations.

properties.date_enacted: Commissioners directed staff to draft the ordinance 2026-07-28; the Board of County Commissioners applied the Pending Ordinance Doctrine and adopted Ordinance No. 26-42 on 2026-09-22 (first noticed for public hearing 2026-09-04; Planning Commission review 2026-09-17).
properties.duration: Twelve-month moratorium on submission and acceptance of applications for building permits, site plans, development orders, development agreements, special permit uses, rezonings, and comprehensive plan amendments related to 'Data Center Facilities' in unincorporated Manatee County, or until repealed, whichever occurs first; may be extended by Board resolution.
properties.trigger: SB 484 (effective 2026-07-01) established local authority over large-load customers; county's land development code and comprehensive plan do not adequately address data centers.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners voted 4-1 on the substantive motion, then 5-0 on a subsequent procedural vote to adopt the ordinance, at a public hearing 2026-09-15/16 (hearing held 2026-09-15 at the McPherson Governmental Campus; reported 2026-09-16).
properties.duration: 12-month (365-day) moratorium on accepting or processing applications for major commercial data centers, AI processing hubs, and cryptocurrency-mining operations, applying to development permits, site plans, rezonings, and conditional-use permits; exempts smaller facilities using under 50 megawatts, which may still proceed through the county's standard Special Use Permit process.
properties.trigger: Concerns over water consumption from the Floridan Aquifer (including Outstanding Florida Springs Silver Springs and Rainbow Springs), power-grid strain, noise, and county staff's stated lack of readiness/criteria to evaluate large data-center applications; balanced against a proposed roughly $10 billion facility that proponents said could generate significant tax revenue and jobs.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted on final hearing 2026-06-08 by the Nassau County Board of County Commissioners (motion by Commissioner Gray, seconded by Commissioner Farmer, approved); first reading was 2026-05-11, following direction to draft on 2026-04-13.
properties.duration: 12 months from the effective date, or until an ordinance amending the Comprehensive Plan, Land Development Regulations, and/or Code of Ordinances relating to Data Center Facilities takes effect, whichever occurs first (Ordinance 2026-044, Section 6). Effective date is upon filing with the Florida Secretary of State per s. 125.66.
properties.trigger: Board directed staff to draft the moratorium in April 2026 to allow time to study and adopt comprehensive-plan and land-development-code provisions for data centers before accepting further applications; a companion resolution (2026-102) created a Fact-Finding Committee on Data Center Development that met repeatedly through June 2026.

properties.date_enacted: City Commission voted 4-1 to advance the ordinance on first reading 2026-09-08 (after a nearly seven-hour public hearing beginning 2026-08-31); adopted on second and final reading by a 3-2 vote 2026-09-22 (Commissioners Stokes, Langdon and Mayor Emrich in favor; Commissioners Petrow and Duval against).
properties.duration: 18-month moratorium on the acceptance and approval of new data-center applications. As finally adopted, the ordinance excludes (does not apply to) the roughly 896,000-square-foot data-center facility already proposed for the Yorkshire-area 'Deep Park' development: staff may still accept, process and review that application, but the city cannot approve it without a City Commission vote. The ordinance also allows any developer to request an 'extraordinary hardship' exception (e.g., permits already issued, substantial expenditure already made), decided case-by-case by the Commission.
properties.trigger: A roughly 896,000 sq ft ('Deep Park') data-center application, part of a larger 282-acre mixed-use development, submitted 2026-07-20 after a non-disclosure agreement (entered August 2025) expired; hundreds of residents packed multiple public hearings (2026-08-31 and 2026-09-22) in opposition, citing water, noise, and infrastructure concerns.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners approved zoning in progress effective 2026-07-07 and directed staff to prepare a formal moratorium ordinance.
properties.duration: Interim administrative freeze: staff directed not to accept new large-load-customer data center applications until a formal ordinance is presented for adoption. The contemplated formal ordinance would run until the earlier of one year after its adoption or the enactment of permanent regulations.
properties.trigger: Followed opposition to Project Tango and other large-load data center proposals.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted on second/final reading by the City Commission 2026-09-23 (Ordinance 3313); first public hearing held 2026-09-08.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on new data center proposals, giving city staff 12 months to study impacts and develop permanent zoning rules; does not apply to existing facilities or routine maintenance.
properties.trigger: Regulatory-gap/precautionary; part of a wave of Bay County-area moratoria.

properties.date_enacted: Commissioners unanimously approved 2026-07-14, following a Planning Commission recommendation 2026-06-11 and a first BOCC hearing 2026-06-16.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium pausing covered development approvals for server or computer rooms exceeding 2.5 MW in unincorporated Pasco County while the county studies definitions and environmental, utility, and financial impacts.

properties.date_enacted: First reading passed 7-0 on 2026-07-16; adopted on second and final reading by a 7-0 vote at the 2026-08-13 City Council Regular Meeting as Ordinance No. 11-26 (agenda item 'Proposed Ordinance No. 13-26').
properties.duration: Proposed one-year moratorium on city approvals for data centers and other large-load-customer facilities with anticipated monthly peak demand of at least 50 MW; would take effect five business days after final adoption.

properties.date_enacted: Placed on first reading 2026-07-21; adopted unanimously at the 2026-08-11 public hearing as Ordinance 2026-22.
properties.duration: Proposed one-year moratorium on data center approvals.
properties.trigger: Followed American Tower's May 2026 filing to redevelop an industrial property at 10700 76th Court N. into a data-processing facility.

properties.date_enacted: Adopted at a special meeting 2026-07-23, following a first hearing 2026-07-09 (which followed a 2026-06-22 3-1 vote directing staff to draft the ordinance).
properties.duration: 12-month moratorium on large-scale data centers and large-load-customer facilities in unincorporated Santa Rosa County; permanent rules may be developed sooner than the 12-month endpoint.
properties.trigger: Several residents requested a permanent ban instead of a temporary moratorium.

properties.date_enacted: County commissioners voted 2026-07-08.
properties.duration: Halts acceptance, review, and approval of hyperscale data center proposals for at least one year, through July 2027, while staff evaluates permanent rules.
properties.trigger: Followed an XF Group inquiry concerning a site along Cattlemen Road; covers facilities at the state-law threshold of at least 50 MW.

properties.date_enacted: Board of County Commissioners voted unanimously to approve the moratorium 2026-08-20 (Thursday), following a public hearing.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on data-center development in unincorporated Washington County (municipalities Chipley, Wausau, and Caryville are not covered, as they control their own development). A facility is defined as a data center if more than 5% of a building's gross floor area is used for computer systems/hardware/racks, in addition to an electrical-usage threshold, with anti-fragmentation language to prevent splitting a project across smaller buildings. May be extended by a further ordinance if permanent regulations are not ready in time.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap; county comprehensive plan and land development code do not adequately address data-center infrastructure and public-safety impacts.

properties.date_enacted: Final approval 2026-06-22 by City Council, following a unanimous first reading 2026-06-08.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium on city approvals for data centers, large-scale data centers, and large-load customer facilities.
properties.trigger: Precautionary measure; city staff said no data center proposal was pending at the time of adoption.

properties.duration: 180 days
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap

properties.duration: 12 months, with an option to extend an additional 6 months
properties.trigger: Growing statewide concern about data center development, following consideration of 180-day, 12-month, and 18-month options

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-04, Appling County Board of Commissioners resolution signed by the Chairman and attested by the County Clerk
properties.duration: 40 days from adoption (to about 2026-09-13), unless lifted earlier or regulations adopted; extendable after a public hearing
properties.trigger: County code, development regulations and zoning do not address data center facilities

properties.duration: Initial moratorium through 2026-03-06; extended through 2026-06-05 by Ordinance 26-03-19 (2026-03-03); replaced 2026-04-07
properties.trigger: Existing zoning did not specifically address data centers; concerns about utilities, contamination, water, and land use

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-02 (Augusta Commission imposed a 49-day pause on new data centers at its Tuesday June 2, 2026 meeting, per same-day WRDW reporting); 2026-07-21 (Commission unanimously extended by 60 days and required three community hearings before any vote on permanent rules)
properties.duration: Initial 49 days from 2026-06-02; extended 60 days on 2026-07-21 (running to approximately 2026-09-19)
properties.trigger: Ongoing consideration of a permanent data-center ordinance; extension adds three public hearings before any vote

properties.date_enacted: Ball Ground City Council vote in mid-August 2026 (reported 2026-08-17)
properties.duration: Not stated in accessible sources
properties.trigger: Give staff time to draft data center regulations, following Cherokee County's moratorium

properties.date_enacted: Banks County Board of Commissioners approved a data center moratorium in August 2026 (reported 2026-08-16); extended at a September 2026 meeting through 2027-03-09
properties.duration: Initial term not stated in accessible text; extended through 2027-03-09
properties.trigger: Update county code to address data centers

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-20, Bloomingdale City Council, unanimous (Thursday meeting), Resolution No. 2026-012
properties.duration: Through 11:59 p.m. on 2027-02-16 (about six months)
properties.trigger: OpenAI's Project Camellia in neighboring Effingham County; protect residents' access to power and water

properties.duration: Original 90-day term (to 2026-05-02) extended by Board action (FA040-2026, 2026-05-04); per the July 6, 2026 regular-meeting minutes the moratorium remains in effect until 2026-12-31.
properties.trigger: County wanted fact-finding time on safety concerns and regulation of data center facilities

properties.duration: Extended to Dec. 31, 2026 (from the original 90-day term) per the May 5, 2026 vote, unless the Board acts sooner.
properties.trigger: Data centers were not listed as permitted or conditional uses; county sought time to decide whether to prohibit or regulate them

properties.date_enacted: 2026-04-27 (Calhoun City Council unanimously passed a 90-day preemptive moratorium resolution at its Monday April 27, 2026 meeting, running through at least July 27); extended six additional months by unanimous (3-0) council vote on 2026-06-08 after a public hearing
properties.duration: Extended through the second council meeting in January 2027, identified in the minutes as 2027-01-25
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap

properties.date_enacted: May 5, 2026 (Tuesday), per GPB/The Current reporting on the Camden County Board of Commissioners meeting, which is corroborated by the earlier May 2, 2026 article reporting the vote was scheduled for 'Tuesday.'
properties.duration: 6 months
properties.trigger: Growing statewide concern about energy-hungry data center operations, amid a contemporaneous Kingsland rezone vote

properties.date_enacted: Board of Commissioners approved a 100-day moratorium on data center and battery energy storage system permits in unincorporated Carroll County at its March 3, 2026 meeting (7-0); extended for another 100 days at the June 3, 2026 meeting (7-0).
properties.duration: 100 days from March 3, 2026 (or until zoning revisions adopted); extended 100 days on June 3, 2026; a third 100-day moratorium approved 7-0 on August 4, 2026, running to approximately 2026-11-12.
properties.trigger: Significant surge in planning, development, and construction of data centers and battery energy storage facilities nationally and in Georgia; the county's zoning ordinance (from the 1990s) did not contemplate these uses.

properties.date_enacted: Cedartown City Commission unanimously approved Resolution 4, 2026 at its March 23, 2026 meeting.
properties.duration: Six months per the city manager's public statement ahead of the vote.
properties.trigger: City wanted time to study how other jurisdictions were regulating data centers before adopting its own rules.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21, Chamblee City Council regular meeting, unanimous
properties.duration: 180 days, through 2027-01-16
properties.trigger: Review code after DeKalb County rejected proposed data center standards (June 23); energy, water, tree canopy, stormwater, noise concerns

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-11, Chatham County Board of Commissioners, unanimous vote at a Friday meeting
properties.duration: 155 days, expiring 2027-02-16; may be extended by up to 60 days
properties.trigger: OpenAI's $20B Effingham County project; county lacks rules addressing large data centers' electricity, water and residential compatibility

properties.duration: Initial 30 days (adopted 2026-07-21/22); extended by 180 days on 2026-08-18, for a total of about 210 days, running through approximately mid-February 2027 (2027-02-14) unless ended early or extended.
properties.trigger: Growing statewide concern about data center development; county plans a public hearing to consider a longer extension

properties.duration: 120 days, through 2025-12-31; extended a total of three times since September 2025 per county documents cited by WABE (July 24, 2026); still in effect as of that date. Exact current end date not confirmed.
properties.trigger: Health, safety, water-supply, and resident concerns after recent approvals

properties.duration: Initial 180 days from 2026-02-24; extended another six months by resolution adopted 2026-08-11, expiring 2027-02-24.
properties.trigger: Surge of metro Atlanta data centers and concern over infrastructure impacts

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-02, Colquitt County Commission, unanimous (motion by Commissioner Johnny Hardin)
properties.duration: 120 days from 2026-06-02 (to about 2026-10-01); extended another 180 days on 2026-09-01
properties.trigger: Allow revision of the zoning ordinance to regulate data centers (industrial/light industrial conditional use)

properties.duration: Originally until 2026-07-04; extended by council action to Aug. 4, 2026 (per the June 1, 2026 agenda) and again to Oct. 20, 2026 (per the July 6, 2026 agenda), before being superseded by the permanent data center ordinance adopted Aug. 17, 2026.
properties.trigger: New annexation and development requests; concern that data centers were treated by-right in industrial zones

properties.date_enacted: May 6, 2025 (180-day moratorium), per news coverage of the Board of Commissioners meeting (4-1 vote, Chairman Bill McKenzie dissenting).
properties.duration: 180 days, expiring 2025-11-03 (per Coweta County spokesperson statement quoted in GPB 2025-10-22)
properties.trigger: Project Peach, Project Sail, petitions, and need for countywide standards

properties.date_enacted: Coweta County Board of Commissioners, unanimous vote at its Tuesday night meeting (2026-06-16) on a 180-day moratorium to review the county's data center ordinance
properties.duration: 180 days (to about 2026-12-13)
properties.trigger: Review of the county's data center ordinance (on-site power generation, cap on number of data centers) with five data centers already proposed

properties.date_enacted: 2026-01-06, Crawford County Board of Commissioners, unanimous (after Planning & Zoning vote 2025-12-18); extended 5-0 on 2026-05-21 to 2026-10-01
properties.trigger: Conduct impact and health studies and draft ordinances

properties.duration: Initial 100 days; extended multiple times, including June 9, 2026 (100 days, to Sept. 30, 2026) and July 7, 2026 (to March 30, 2027, per Board resolution).
properties.trigger: Public health, diesel emissions, water, stormwater, noise, and ratepayer concerns

properties.duration: Indefinite
properties.trigger: Proactive planning before possible future projects

properties.duration: Initial 45 days from 2026-07-20; extended up to 180 days by resolution at a special called meeting 2026-08-31, through 2027-02-27 unless ended sooner or new zoning regulations become effective.
properties.trigger: Growing statewide concern about data center development

properties.date_enacted: March 18, 2025 (Resolution No. 25-116)
properties.duration: Up to 90 days
properties.trigger: Proposal pipeline and need to update comprehensive plan and unified development code

properties.date_enacted: Original enactment date not confirmed in this pass; City Council extended an existing moratorium by three months on 2026-06-15
properties.duration: Extended three months (approximately 90 days) by voice vote

properties.duration: 90 days
properties.trigger: Applications for annexation, rezoning, variances, and conceptual site plans for data centers

properties.duration: 80 days
properties.trigger: Allow work on an ordinance and a process requiring a public hearing for each future data center proposal

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-31, Forest Park City Council special called meeting (Monday)
properties.duration: 90 days (to about 2026-11-29)
properties.trigger: Time to draft zoning changes; Digital Realty campus at former Fort Gillem already approved in the city

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-06, Franklin County Board of Commissioners, unanimous (Commissioner Pulliam and Chair Long absent), following a June 30 work session
properties.duration: Until 2026-12-08 (shortened from a proposed six months on counsel's advice)
properties.trigger: No county regulations for data centers; commissioners concerned about farmland; county attorney recommended a temporary moratorium while permanent regulations are drafted

properties.duration: 6 months, effective immediately
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap

properties.date_enacted: 2026-02-03 (Gordon County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to place a moratorium on construction of data centers while updating the ULDC); extended through 2027-01-29 by resolution at the 2026-07-07 regular meeting
properties.duration: Extended through 2027-01-29
