properties.trigger: Pause on development, building, site-plan, variance, stormwater, conditional-use, occupancy, public-utility, and large-load electric applications for data centers while the City Manager studies recommendations

properties.duration: One year from passage
properties.trigger: Public opposition to a proposed data center, concern that data centers were treated as warehouse uses under Chapter 400, and concerns about water consumption, power consumption, noise, and other effects.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-20 (City Council, 8-0)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Pause on accepting and processing applications for new data center development, construction, or expansion while the city studies regulation

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-14 (Board of Aldermen, 7-0, one absent)
properties.duration: No longer than one year; may end earlier by board action or upon adoption of permanent standards
properties.trigger: Pause on review and approval of zoning amendments, site plans, special use permits, and building permits for information technology and data processing facilities while the city studies regulation

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-22 (Jackson County Legislature final passage vote, 8 in favor and 1 excused). Per KCTV5, the measure then went to County Executive Phil LeVota, who had 10 days to sign or veto; no veto was reported in any subsequent coverage found in this pass, but independent confirmation of the Executive's signature was not obtained.
properties.duration: 180 days, amended up from the original 120-day Ordinance 6074 proposal introduced 2026-04-06 by Legislator Sean E. Smith. The Legislature had also been considering a competing 365-day version (Ordinance 6087, sponsored by Legislative Chair Manny Abarca) before settling on the 180-day term that passed 8-1 on 2026-06-22.
properties.trigger: Rapid emergence of data center and battery energy storage system applications; perceived gaps in the Jackson County Unified Development Code; infrastructure, environmental, public safety, and public notice concerns.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-15 (County Commission, unanimous)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Planning and Zoning Commission recommended the pause so the county could consider amendments to its land-use order

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21 (County Commission order)
properties.duration: Six months, with one extension of up to six additional months permitted upon written findings
properties.trigger: Pause on data center construction, conversion, establishment, new operation, expansion, and related permits in unincorporated Nodaway County

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-23 (Ralls County Commission, signed at a Sunday courthouse meeting per WGEM's same-day report and Muddy River News)
properties.duration: Approximately one year, to September 1, 2027
properties.trigger: Commissioners moved after learning (from a tenant's report and, separately, from the county's electric cooperative) that a property owner along Mo. Highway 19 near Center may be negotiating to sell roughly 53 acres to a data center company; commissioners said they wanted time to study the issue before any project could be 'grandfathered in.'

properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Pause on approvals for larger data centers (exceeding 5 MW, 100,000 square feet, or multiple buildings on a campus) while county studies health, safety, infrastructure, and regulatory issues

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-04 (Stone County Commission signed the Order and Ordinance enacting the moratorium, per Commission minutes; based on a Stone County Planning Commission resolution adopted 2026-06-02).
properties.duration: 12 months from the effective date
properties.trigger: Stone County Planning Commission cited 'considerable interest and concern on the part of residents' about possible development of solar, wind, battery-storage, and data-center projects in unincorporated Stone County, and sought time to consider amendments to the county Zoning Regulations.

properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: County study of legal authority and potential impacts of data centers, solar, wind, and battery energy storage system facilities in unincorporated Webster County

properties.duration: As proposed (not yet adopted): a six-month moratorium on data center construction, with up to two additional one-year extensions available, after which the Council of Commissioners would be required to enact permanent regulations. At its 2026-09-02 meeting, the Butte-Silver Bow Council of Commissioners voted 11-0 to direct the county attorney to prepare a temporary moratorium/interim zoning ordinance draft; no draft ordinance had been brought back for a final adoption vote as of 2026-09-23.
properties.trigger: Ongoing local debate over data center development, including a separately litigated local ballot initiative (406 People First / Local Initiative 00-02) to require voter approval of data centers, a pending Montana Supreme Court appeal over that initiative's ballot eligibility, and public testimony citing power-supply concerns tied to a still-pending Montana Public Service Commission large-load tariff proceeding.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-09 (Board of County Commissioners unanimous adoption after a public hearing)
properties.duration: One year from adoption (2026-07-09 to 2027-07-08), or until replaced sooner by permanent zoning
properties.trigger: County commissioners directed to study an asserted emergency and possible mitigation measures related to data center development pressure in unincorporated county areas

properties.date_enacted: 2026-03-16, Butler County Board of Supervisors, 4-1 roll-call vote (Griess, Vandenberg, Bauer, Steager aye; Krafka nay)
properties.duration: 9 months from adoption (2026-03-16)
properties.trigger: Butler County has no zoning; a countywide survey (~800 responses) found roughly 90% support for a moratorium on the top land uses of concern (wind, solar, data centers, battery storage, landfill), following years of unregulated development including the in-progress Sandhills Energy solar project.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-11, Cass County Board of Commissioners, 5-0 unanimous vote, motion by District 4 Commissioner Daniel Stohlmann
properties.duration: 12 months (a 'baseline' minimum per Commissioner Alexander DeGarmo, extendable if more time is needed, or endable early if regulations are adopted sooner)
properties.trigger: specific_project trigger (Tenaska/Google-linked proposal: Tenaska optioned 1,354 acres in Cass County along Highway 75 south of Murray and Beaver Lake for a data center/natural-gas power plant project) combined with a regulatory gap; a separate set of proposed zoning regulations was tabled to Sept. 22, 2026 for further discussion.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Commissioners voted 2-1 on 2026-07-14 to impose a moratorium, effective that day.
properties.duration: Six-month moratorium on all conditional use permits (broader than data centers), adopted amid board discussion focused on the county's lack of data center provisions. No separate ordinance or resolution text was located; recorded as a motion in the minutes.
properties.trigger: County zoning rules did not address data centers; disagreement among commissioners about whether Nebraska law clearly authorizes such a moratorium.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-23, Fillmore County Board of Supervisors, 6-1 roll-call vote
properties.duration: 6 months from the date of approval (2026-06-23)
properties.trigger: Resident concerns raised at public comment about health, safety, and property-value impacts of proposed solar energy farms.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-16, Gage County Board of Supervisors, motion by Supervisor Rex Adams
properties.duration: 12 months from 2026-09-16, superseding an earlier 8-month moratorium the Board had passed in August 2026; the Planning and Zoning Commission had recommended an 18-month term after a crowded June 2026 public hearing, but the Board adopted 12 months instead.
properties.trigger: County has no data-center-specific regulations; Board wanted time to develop them following a contested public process (a June 2026 Planning and Zoning Commission hearing drew 170+ people and a Sept. 3, 2026 supervisors' hearing drew 120+ people, most urging an 18-month or longer term).

properties.duration: One year or until updated zoning regulations were adopted, whichever was less
properties.trigger: Existing zoning did not adequately address data centers and crypto mining in AG-G and RCI districts. The resolution cited energy consumption, cooling and environmental footprint concerns, land-use impacts, and the need to study countywide zoning controls.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-21; proposed Resolution 26-18 was on the Sept. 8, 2026 Board of Commissioners agenda (item 9) and discussed again at the Sept. 21, 2026 meeting, where the minutes record 'Discussion held on proposed Resolution 26-18. No action taken at this time.'
properties.duration: Proposed 12 months
properties.trigger: Regulatory-gap/preemptive: county attorney and chair described ongoing work to update the county's comprehensive plan and zoning regulations (targeted for completion by May 2027) and encouraged public participation in town-hall meetings on the update; the proposed moratorium would pause applications while that update is completed.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Commissioners voted 3-0 to adopt Resolution 26-2 on 2026-07-15.
properties.duration: 12-month moratorium on accepting applications for data centers and AI facilities, cryptocurrency mining, wind and solar energy systems, battery energy storage, carbon dioxide facilities, future high-voltage transmission infrastructure, and other utility-scale or specialized-technology facilities.
properties.trigger: Adopted alongside a wave of Nebraska county moratoria addressing data centers and related utility-scale/specialized-technology development.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-10, McPherson County Board of Commissioners, unanimous vote (Nason, Arensdorf, Chairman Bryant)
properties.duration: 12 months from 2026-06-10; the Board reserved exclusive authority to extend it. Resolution 2026-11 expressly supersedes prior county moratorium Resolutions 2025-19, 2025-21, and 2025-25, indicating the county has maintained some form of moratorium on these uses since at least 2025.
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap: broad pause covering utility-scale and specialized technology facilities pending county zoning/regulatory development.

properties.duration: Moratorium on building and conditional-use permits for data centers, for up to one year from adoption (i.e., through on or about 2027-05-19), and subject to earlier termination if the zoning review committee's updated regulations are approved sooner.
properties.trigger: Large public response and concern over potential health, environmental, and community-fit impacts of data centers.

properties.duration: 12 months (2025-09-22 to 2026-09-22); extended for an additional 12 months by Resolution No. 1612, Book 25, Page 2, adopted 2026-08-24.
properties.trigger: The captured board minutes record adoption but do not include detailed findings. Later local discussion in earlier captures referenced noise and public-power/rate implications.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Commissioners adopted Resolution 3937 on 2026-06-30, effective immediately, with three affirmative votes and two members absent.
properties.duration: Pauses data center construction, building permits, conditional use permits, and any other project authorization. Expires at the earlier of 12 months or the effective date of new data center zoning regulations, unless extended by a separate resolution.
properties.trigger: County had discussed a draft moratorium after a commissioner proposed a pause; adopted while the county develops permanent data center zoning regulations.

properties.date_enacted: 2023-08-01, Seward County Board of Commissioners (original adoption); most recently continued by Resolution No. 3947, adopted 2026-08-25
properties.duration: Originally a 6-month moratorium adopted 2023-08-01, repeatedly continued/renewed by separate board resolutions (including at the Jan. 6, 2026 meeting) for further 6-month terms or until new zoning regulations are formally adopted, whichever occurs first; most recently continued by Resolution No. 3947 (2026-08-25) for 6 months from that date.
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap: the county's zoning regulations do not yet address commercial-scale renewable energy systems; the moratorium is intended to remain in place only until new zoning regulations governing such systems are formally adopted and become legally binding.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-26, Fallon Business Council, per the meeting agenda item 'Data Center Ban - Resolution #26-F-112' (agenda item filed by Chairman Phil Johnson) at the Fallon Business Council Regular Meeting 2
properties.duration: Permanent; no stated end date or review/sunset provision found.
properties.trigger: Preemptive protection of tribal water and land resources; tribal council secretary Phil Johnson introduced the resolution.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-06, Humboldt County Commission, unanimous vote on second reading of Bill No. 05-18-26 (one local news account describes the meeting as occurring July 7)
properties.duration: Through July 13, 2027 (amended at the meeting)
properties.trigger: Precautionary pause pending regulation; no data center proposal or development application was pending when the measure passed

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-02 (Nye County Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved a countywide moratorium on new data center applications at its Tuesday, June 2, 2026 meeting, per Pahrump Valley Times)
properties.duration: No fixed term; Commissioner Strickland was quoted estimating a new data center ordinance could be ready 'in about 90 days,' but the moratorium's stated end condition is adoption of local data center regulations, not a calendar date.
properties.trigger: Nye County Water District Governing Board's 2026-05-27 emergency request that the commission impose a moratorium, driven by concerns over data center water demand on a 'critically over-appropriated' aquifer (Nevada Hydrographic Basin 162) in the Pahrump Regional Planning District

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-21, Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribal Council vote
properties.duration: Permanent; no stated end date found.
properties.trigger: Protection of Pyramid Lake water resources and the endangered Cui-ui and threatened Lahontan cutthroat trout from upstream Truckee River watershed data center water demand; concerns about grid reliability given existing rolling brownouts on the reservation. Began as a community-led proposal to the Tribal Council.

properties.date_enacted: Reno City Council approved a final moratorium resolution on/around 2026-06-01, extending an earlier temporary pause on special-use permits for new data centers through August 31, 2027, by a 6-1 vote (Councilmember Kathleen Taylor dissenting). Coverage headlines describe this both as an 'extension' of an existing pause and as the council 'approving' the moratorium, consistent with an initial shorter pause enacted earlier in 2026 that was then extended.
properties.duration: Runs through August 31, 2027, or until the city adopts new data center regulations, whichever comes first.
properties.trigger: Concerns over water use and rising power costs from new data center development

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-23, Wells City Council, unanimous vote (4-0, Councilman Richard Peltier absent) on Resolution No. 26-06
properties.duration: 12 months from the effective date (adoption), unless earlier repealed, modified, extended, or superseded by Council action.
properties.trigger: Preemptive/precautionary pause; city stated no data center projects were proposed or approved in Wells at adoption, but wanted time to study land use, infrastructure, water, electricity, noise, and emergency-response impacts before any proposal arrives.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-22, White Pine County Board of County Commissioners, adopted at a duly noticed public meeting (per the signed resolution's adoption clause)
properties.duration: 180 calendar days from the effective date (adoption), renewable by Board resolution for one additional period of up to 180 days after a noticed public hearing.
properties.trigger: Preemptive pause after White Pine County was identified at an April 24, 2026 Nevada Legislature Joint Interim Committee on Public Lands meeting as a target for data center development (with BLM officials present), combined with concerns over the Steptoe Valley aquifer, limited rural electric infrastructure, and the lack of data-center-specific zoning standards in Title 17.

properties.date_enacted: Planning Board voted 5-0-0 on 2026-07-01 to adopt and advance the proposed ordinance; Nottingham voters ratified it at a September 8, 2026 special town election (held with the state primary) by a vote of 1,335 to 143, per the town's official election results.
properties.duration: 12 months from voter adoption on 2026-09-08 (to approximately 2027-09-08).
properties.trigger: Local opposition to a withdrawn Nottingham Business Park data center concept (145 Old Turnpike Road) and an online petition that drew more than 25,000 signatures

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-16 was the ordinance's introduction/first reading (per the June 16, 2026 Council agenda listing Ordinance 2172-2026 for public hearing). Final passage occurred at the July 14, 2026 Council meeting (per that meeting's official agenda/ordinance statements) and the Township's public notice titled 'Publication Final Passage Ordinance #2172-2026 Temporary Moratorium of Data Centers' was posted July 15, 2026.
properties.duration: Six months (180 days) while the Planning Board and Environmental Commission study data centers
properties.trigger: Planning Board and Environmental Commission to study data center land use and make recommendations before further approvals proceed

properties.date_enacted: Introduced (first reading) August 25, 2026 by the Mullica Township Committee; referred to the Planning Board and Environmental Commission for study and recommendation, as required before final adoption; not yet finally passed as of the September 22, 2026 Committee meeting agenda, which does not list it for second reading.
properties.duration: Six (6) months from final adoption, if adopted as introduced.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap; the Township referred the question to its Planning Board and Environmental Commission to study infrastructure, water, noise, stormwater, traffic, zoning, and emergency-response impacts before any data center could be approved.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-20, Borough Council second and final reading following a public hearing
properties.duration: 18 months from adoption; the ordinance also requires publication and mayoral approval, and the copy reviewed does not show the mayoral approval date
properties.trigger: Study of electric-grid, water, stormwater, fiscal, land-use, noise, and environmental effects of data center development

properties.date_enacted: Reported adopted 'late last month' (late August 2026) per CPR.org's September 3, 2026 article; a public hearing on the proposed ordinance was held August 11, 2026 and the county's own public notice states the Board of Commissioners could consider adoption at its August 25, 2026 meeting.
properties.duration: One year from adoption (to approximately 2027-08-25).
properties.trigger: Concern over water use during a severe/extreme drought affecting the county, plus concerns about energy use, heat, and noise; came after the City of Raton's since-expired memorandum of understanding with a data-center developer (Atterix LLC) drew controversy.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-30, Board of County Commissioners, 5-0 vote
properties.duration: 18 months, immediate; amended during the meeting from an original 12-month proposal
properties.trigger: Development of permanent standards addressing groundwater, electricity and grid reliability, noise, waste heat, environmental justice, monitoring, and public participation

properties.date_enacted: Reportedly 2026-07-21, Board of County Commissioners, unanimous vote amending agenda item Resolution 2026-51 during the meeting
properties.duration: 18 months from adoption (2026-07-21), to approximately 2028-01-21, confirmed by Resolution No. 2026-51 as named in KRQE and gpkmedia.com/Sierra County Sentinel reporting and listed on the Sierra County Clerk's resolutions index.
properties.trigger: Concern about a possible data center at Spaceport America

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-09, unanimous vote of the Socorro County Board of Commissioners.
properties.duration: One year from adoption (to approximately 2027-06-09).
properties.trigger: Public opposition to a proposed roughly 10,000-acre solar-plus-data-center facility ("Green Data Center" project) and concerns over water rights/use, energy infrastructure, and public safety; commission appointed a 15-member Blue Ribbon Committee (named 2026-07-29 from 35 applicants) to study these issues and deliver non-binding recommendations at least two months before the moratorium expires.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-24, Town Board, following a June 24, 2026 public hearing (public hearing originally set at the May 27, 2026 meeting by unanimous vote)
properties.duration: Twelve (12) months
properties.trigger: General, preemptive townwide pause. Town Supervisor David VanLuven said a moratorium is not a final fix and that the town needs to identify what protective measures it can legally adopt.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet enacted as of 2026-09-23. Buffalo Common Council members were reported September 22, 2026 to be moving a proposed two-year moratorium on new data centers and cryptocurrency facilities toward a full Council vote 'set for next Tuesday' (on or about 2026-09-29).
properties.duration: Proposed two years.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap and infrastructure capacity; Councilmember Golombek cited the need to update zoning before more facilities are developed and to ensure new projects do not strain neighborhood water and sewer infrastructure without a community benefit agreement.

properties.date_enacted: Approved by the Clay Town Board on or shortly before 2026-06-30 (date of first news coverage), following a public hearing
properties.duration: Up to twelve (12) months
properties.trigger: Preemptive townwide pause tied to anticipated development pressure around Micron Technology's planned semiconductor campus in neighboring areas; no data center projects had been proposed in Clay as of adoption.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-15, East Greenbush Town Board, unanimous vote, following a July 8, 2026 public hearing
properties.duration: Base term of six (6) months from the effective date (filing with the NY Secretary of State); if the Town Board passes a resolution extending it before expiration, the moratorium may run up to one (1) year total from the effective date.
properties.trigger: General, preemptive townwide pause; Town Supervisor Jack Conway cited concerns about a possible legal challenge to Governor Hochul's Executive Order 62 and a desire for an independent local 'layer of protection' against data center development.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet enacted as of 2026-09-23. On 2026-05-13 the Town Board adopted a resolution directing the Planning Board to draft data center legislation. A draft moratorium local law (modeled on Newfield's) was rewritten twice between July and mid-August 2026 on the advice of Town legal counsel Guy Krogh. At its August 12, 2026 meeting the Town Board did NOT set a public hearing as previously expected; it instead held off action, pushing back the hearing and the law's adoption to October 2026 at the earliest.
properties.duration: Proposed as a one-year moratorium in the draft local law circulating as of July-August 2026.
properties.trigger: Preemptive; no data center has been proposed in Enfield, but officials cited the town's lack of zoning, limited water and electric infrastructure, concern that 'satellite data centers' could arise near TeraWulf's proposed Lansing project, and the regional wave of moratoria (notably Newfield's) as reasons to act.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet enacted as of 2026-09-23. At its meeting of 2026-09-15 (following an August 18, 2026 initial discussion), the Town Board voted unanimously (motion by Councilman Michael Robbins, seconded by Supervisor Peter Goodman) to direct Town Attorney Benjamin Gailey to prepare a proposed local law establishing a data center moratorium; that draft law will require its own future public hearing before formal adoption, expected 'within the next couple of meetings' as of September 15.
properties.duration: Not yet fixed; Town Attorney Benjamin Gailey told the Board such local laws are 'usually effective for 12 to 18 months, but provisions can extend them,' and the Board discussed a possible timeline of at least a year. Some residents urged a permanent moratorium/ban instead.
properties.trigger: Preemptive; the town had no pending data center applications as of the September 15 meeting, but officials and residents wanted to study electricity and water usage, and impacts on the local Bashakill wetlands, before any proposal arrives.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-09 -- Town Board vote, 7-0.
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Concerns about rising utility bills and outages, water supply, and environmental impact from data processing centers and commercial cryptocurrency mining.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-09, Town Board, unanimous vote, following a public hearing that evening (proposed at the June 11, 2026 meeting)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: General, preemptive townwide pause; no data center has been proposed in Newfield, but officials cited the town's lack of zoning laws and the regional wave of proposals (notably TeraWulf's Lansing project) as reasons to act before an application arrives.

properties.date_enacted: Original moratorium: Local Law 2024-2, adopted by the Common Council on 2024-07-16 (a two-year moratorium on cryptocurrency mining and data processing centers, set to expire 2026-07-16). Extension: a 2026 local law extending the moratorium for an additional 12 months from its new effective date, adopted before the July 16, 2026 expiration.
properties.duration: Original term: two years (2024-07-16 to 2026-07-16) under Local Law 2024-2. 2026 extension: an additional twelve (12) months from the extension's effective date.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: the city's November 18, 2025 Comprehensive Plan update was completed but zoning amendments and recommendations specific to cryptocurrency mining/data processing centers were not yet finalized, prompting an extension rather than letting the original moratorium lapse.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-04, Town Board, per the Rockefeller Institute of Government's tracking blog and Leader Herald (dailygazette.com) headline coverage
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: General, preemptive townwide pause; Town Supervisor Greg Fagan cited concerns over energy usage and a desire to maintain local control, ahead of possible state legislative action.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-03, Town Board, unanimous vote, following an August 3, 2026 public hearing
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Specific project: a proposed 300 MW, ~500,000-square-foot, ~$2 billion data center by Riverview Innovation & Technology Campus at the former Tonawanda Coke Corp. industrial site on River Road, which drew sustained resident opposition over environmental, noise, and utility-cost concerns (the site is near the former Love Canal-adjacent area of concern residents cited).

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-16 (Town Board, unanimous, following a public hearing)
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: Pause on all new data-center applications to allow the planning department to develop comprehensive zoning rules on location, design, operation, infrastructure, energy and water use, noise, visual effects, environmental sustainability, public safety, and efficiency

properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Moratorium on the siting, acceptance, review, and approval of applications for a 'Data Storage Center' within the town

properties.duration: 18 months as initially adopted under Local Law No. 2 of 2024 (2024-07-31 to approximately 2026-01-31); extended to 20 months (through approximately 2026-03-31) by Local Law No. 1 of 2026, which the signed, clerk-filed Local Law Filing shows was duly passed by the Town Board on 2026-01-15 and certified/filed with the NY Department of State on 2026-01-19 (ecode360 filing LF2566760); the extended moratorium was in turn superseded, before its extended term expired, by permanent zoning Local Law No. 2 of 2026, adopted 2026-02-19.
properties.trigger: Proposed commercial cryptocurrency/data-processing use in Freeville area, regulatory gap, and stated concern for natural, historic, cultural, and electrical resources

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-25 (Town Board, unanimous, following a public hearing and a rally outside Town Hall)
properties.duration: Until 2029-07-01, for data centers over 20 MW
properties.trigger: Opposition to a possible 1,000 MW project associated with Treetop Development; the supervisor said no formal application had been filed with the town

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-09 (Town Board, unanimous vote, at the same June 9, 2026 public hearing held at the Town of Highland Senior & Community Center); notice of enactment (Local Law No. 1 of 2026) was subsequently published by the town on 2026-06-18.
properties.duration: 12 months, extendable up to 24 months while zoning and potential impacts are studied
properties.trigger: Pause on approval, permitting, and construction of large-scale data centers while zoning and impacts are studied

properties.jurisdiction: Town of Lansing (Tompkins County) - proposed, not enacted
properties.date_enacted: Not enacted. Public hearing held 2025-09-24; the Town Board's resolution withdrawing the proposed moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025) is confirmed on the November 19, 2025 Town Board meeting agenda (Item 4, Motions and Resolutions: "Resolution Withdrawing Proposed Moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025)").
properties.duration: Proposed 365 days
properties.trigger: Town zoning rewrite and EPOD planning process, plus local concern about large commercial and industrial projects including the TeraWulf Cayuga Data Campus

properties.jurisdiction: Town of Lewiston (Niagara County) - proposed, public hearing held
properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-04-13 by the Town Board (5-0 vote) at its regular work session, immediately following a public hearing that evening, alongside a related zoning-code amendment (Local Law No. 2 of 2026); filed as Local Law No. 3 of 2026 in the Town's official 2026 Local Laws register.
properties.duration: Eighteen (18) months from the effective date of adoption (the 'Moratorium Period'), extendable by Town Board resolution for additional periods not to exceed six months each.
properties.trigger: General/preemptive moratorium. The enacted law's legislative findings (Section 3) cite electrical and wastewater infrastructure capacity, fire safety, the absence of a zoning framework for these uses in the Town Code, and a pending Comprehensive Plan update -- no specific project or applicant is named anywhere in the enacted text.

properties.jurisdiction: Town of Lysander (Onondaga County) - drafting authorized
properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-07 (Town Board, unanimous vote, following a public hearing at Lysander Town Hall attended by more than 350 residents). The Town Supervisor's official 'Data Center Moratorium Updates' notice states: '5/7/2026 - Public Hearing on Local Law #4 ... Moratorium passed. Expires 11/7/26.'
properties.duration: Six (6) months, per Local Law #4 of 2026, 'Six-Month Moratorium on Data Storage Centers.'
properties.trigger: Proposed ~300 MW data center by Ranalli Super DC, LLC (a company controlled by James Ranalli of United Auto Supply) on roughly 120-124 acres of vacant industrial land at the corner of Hencle Boulevard and Oswego Road in Lysander. The developer had spent nearly $1 million on grid-interconnection engineering studies and requested a NYISO transmission connection; roughly 2,600 residents signed a petition urging the Town to adopt a moratorium.

properties.jurisdiction: Town of Oneonta (Otsego County) - proposed, pending
properties.date_enacted: Adopted 2026-05-15 by a unanimous Town Board vote.
properties.duration: Proposed 1 year
properties.trigger: Eco-Yotta Inc. proposal associated with 357 County Road 9 and requested rezoning of about 150 acres of farmland, plus resident opposition

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-27 (Town Board adoption, following public hearing at which no one spoke in opposition)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Moratorium on commercial cryptocurrency mining operations and data processing centers, including AI processing and large-scale data computing, storage, and processing facilities

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-21 (Town Board adoption, following the May 7 public hearing)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Pause on acceptance or further review of building permit and site plan applications for electronic data storage facilities drawing significant electricity from public utilities

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-20 (Town Board, 5-0 roll-call vote, after public hearing)
properties.duration: Two years
properties.trigger: Moratorium on commercial cryptocurrency mining operations and data processing centers; stops acceptance of applications and issuance of permits during the pause

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-03 (Town Board, unanimous)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Moratorium on the development or construction of commercial cryptocurrency mining operations, data mining, data processing centers, and data storage facilities, townwide

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-17, Board of Commissioners unanimous adoption of a one-year moratorium after a public hearing (county attorney's draft had proposed six months, through 2027-02-17; the board lengthened it to a year)
properties.duration: One year (to about 2027-08-17), per the motion as amended
properties.trigger: County ordinances do not address data centers; residents urged a longer pause

properties.date_enacted: Proposed; public hearing and vote on a one-year moratorium resolution postponed from 2026-09-14 to the 2026-10-05 Board of Commissioners meeting
properties.duration: Proposed one year
properties.trigger: Resident concerns about water, energy and farmland

properties.date_enacted: 2023-05-02 effective; extended 2024-05-07 by Ordinance 24-05-09
properties.duration: Original 1 year; extended to 2025-04-30 or earlier adoption of text amendment
properties.trigger: Cryptocurrency mining server farms; county cited electricity use, greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, e-waste, noise, and lack of standards.

properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance does not identify or regulate data centers as a permitted use; adopted proactively as part of a broader wave of Bucks County municipalities (following neighboring Falls Township's contested Amazon data center) acting to define and regulate the use before an application arrives.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-03, East Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors vote to initiate a municipal curative amendment (Chester County); exact day not confirmed in sources reviewed
properties.duration: 180 days from the March 2026 vote to draft and adopt a data-center zoning ordinance ('Data Center Ordinance'); a public hearing to consider its adoption was set for Sept. 24, 2026.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with a specific, highly contested project: developer Green Fig's proposal (later expanded to 1.7 million sq ft) for a data center on Swedesford Road, which drew sustained community opposition; the township already had an earlier, separately approved 2024 data-center plan on the same site.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-27, Falls Township Board of Supervisors vote (Bucks County)
properties.duration: 180 days from July 27, 2026 for the township to review and potentially amend Chapter 209 of its zoning ordinance regarding data centers.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with sustained public opposition to the already-approved Amazon Web Services data center (a 2-million-square-foot, 10-building campus under construction at the former U.S. Steel/Keystone Trade Center site); residents demanded clearer definitions of 'data center' and infrastructure/utility standards for future proposals.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-20, Gregg Township Board of Supervisors, special meeting, unanimous adoption of Resolution 2026-03
properties.duration: Not to exceed 180 days, or until earlier terminated by the Board of Supervisors; bars new data center or 'technical development' applications while a curative amendment to the zoning ordinance is completed. Excludes the pending PNK Group application, which continues to be processed separately.
properties.trigger: Curative-amendment process to add data-center zoning standards, prompted by PNK Group's pending application for a large data-center campus at Great Stream Commons and the absence of applicable standards in the township's zoning ordinance.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-08, Hazle Township (Luzerne County) Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote adopting a curative amendment.
properties.duration: 180 days from adoption (to approximately 2026-12-05).
properties.trigger: Followed sustained community opposition ("Project Hazelnot") to NorthPoint Development's proposed ~1,300-acre, 15-building "Project Hazelnut" data-center campus with substation, which the township had already rejected in November 2025 and which a Luzerne County judge ruled against in spring 2026.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-14, Little Britain Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote adopting the formal moratorium resolution (Lancaster County); preceded by a June 9, 2026 preliminary vote to move forward with the same moratorium concept.
properties.duration: 180 days from the July 14, 2026 resolution, preventing submission of any applications for data centers, their ancillary structures, or energy generation, while the township develops a zoning ordinance.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: the township has no ordinance specifically addressing data centers; adopted proactively while the board develops a new ordinance modeled on those of nearby townships.

properties.date_enacted: County commissioners reportedly approved a curative-amendment resolution on 2026-06-18.
properties.duration: 180-day municipal curative-amendment period after declaring the county zoning ordinance substantially invalid for lacking appropriate regulation of data centers and related uses; affects municipalities participating in the county zoning partnership.
properties.trigger: County zoning ordinance lacked appropriate regulation of data centers and related uses.

properties.duration: 180 days, expiring about 2026-05-17 unless extended or superseded
properties.trigger: Concern over potential data centers or similar large-scale digital/technology facilities; county needed time for Planning Commission ad-hoc committee ordinance work

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21, Morrisville Borough Council, vote to adopt the curative amendment (Bucks County)
properties.duration: 180-day waiting period from July 21, 2026 to review land-use impacts and adopt updated data-center zoning regulations.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap, adopted in the same week as neighboring Falls Township's similar action amid broader Bucks County concern over data-center energy consumption, noise, and water usage.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-18, Mount Carmel Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote (Northumberland County)
properties.duration: 180 days from May 18, 2026 to complete a municipal curative amendment ('Zoning Amendment') addressing data centers.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with sustained community opposition: hundreds of residents packed public meetings (including a May 13, 2026 hearing) opposing data-center development in the township; officials say they cannot outright ban the use but are working to limit and define it through zoning.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Supervisors approved a temporary moratorium at an April 28, 2026 special meeting; reported by the Sun-Gazette on 2026-05-01.
properties.duration: Nine months, or until the township adopts zoning regulations addressing data centers, whichever occurs first. Bars acceptance or review of listed municipal applications for data centers, data center campuses, high-intensity data processing facilities, and substantially similar uses during that period.
properties.trigger: Lack of existing zoning provisions addressing data centers.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-06, Smithfield Township Board of Supervisors, adoption of Resolution No. 621 (Monroe County)
properties.duration: Up to 180 days from May 6, 2026 (statutory ceiling Nov. 2, 2026) to adopt curative zoning amendments for data centers, data center accessory uses, and disaster recovery facilities; the process concluded early when the Board adopted the resulting curative amendment on 2026-08-12.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance did not specifically address data centers; adopted proactively to develop tailored standards and a dedicated zoning district.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05, Upper Burrell Township Board of Supervisors (Westmoreland County); exact day not confirmed in sources reviewed
properties.duration: 180 days; does not apply to building permits already granted to TECfusions for work on its existing 'Building J' (already operational), and did not prevent the township from later approving a land development plan (Aug. 5, 2026) for further electrical/mechanical upgrades to that building. Ends 2026-11-02.
properties.trigger: Public pressure over TECfusions' 'Keystone Connect' hyperscale data-center campus (up to 1,400 acres, potentially up to 3 gigawatts, at the former Alcoa/Arconic Technical Center); residents sought more transparency and regulation before further development.

properties.date_enacted: Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution 2026-09 on 2026-05-13, formally ratifying an administrative pause the township says began with a March 11, 2026 motion.
properties.duration: Pause on applications for data center-related uses while the township prepares tailored zoning standards and pursues a municipal curative amendment. No explicit day count for the pause was located.
properties.trigger: Township preparing tailored zoning standards for data centers.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-15, West Mahanoy Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote (Schuylkill County)
properties.duration: 180 days. Per the adopted resolution's text, the township 'shall not be required to entertain or consider any landowner's curative amendment or proposals for a data center use or solar farm' during that period.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: the zoning ordinance does not explicitly permit or provide standards for data centers or solar farms ('we don't have the protections in place'); adopted proactively, with no application pending, amid data-center and warehouse-development activity in neighboring Butler and Kline townships.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05, West Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors vote to invoke a municipal curative amendment (Chester County); exact day not confirmed, reported to the Planning Commission as already invoked on 2026-05-05
properties.duration: 180 days from adoption to adopt corrective zoning amendments addressing data centers.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance did not address data centers; adopted proactively, with no application pending, following neighboring East Whiteland Township's contested Green Fig data-center dispute.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-09, Williamsport City Council, 6-0 vote adopting Resolution #10088 (Lycoming County)
properties.duration: 180 days from adoption to enact a curative amendment under 53 P.S. Section 10609.2, with a follow-up resolution required within 30 days making specific findings of invalidity. Councilman Milliken characterized it as effectively 'hitting pause' on data-center development even though the resolution does not describe itself as a 'pause.'
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap: 1998 zoning ordinance does not account for data centers or their accessory uses; adopted proactively, following similar curative-amendment action by Lycoming County and several county townships, to close the loophole that would otherwise let a developer file a landowner curative amendment and force approval of a data center anywhere in the city.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-27 (Town Council public hearing and approval by voice vote at its regular meeting)
properties.duration: One year upon passage, or as otherwise provided by the Town Council by ordinance; effective immediately upon passage
properties.trigger: Town's ordinances and zoning regulations are silent on data centers; officials anticipate data center applications given the town's undeveloped land near water bodies and wanted time to draft siting/zoning rules before any application could vest

properties.date_enacted: August 18, 2026 (County Council third reading, per county's own Aug. 18, 2026 agenda packet and Fox Carolina/WYFF4/WSPA coverage of the unanimous-report vote; first reading was a special called meeting June 29, 2026)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: County has no regulatory framework or zoning structure for data centers; concern over strain on the electric power grid, water supply, and local infrastructure from inadequately regulated development of multiple data centers.

properties.date_enacted: July 20, 2026 (County Council unanimous approval, per WSOC-TV, following a June 15, 2026 first reading)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Pause to allow the county to develop rules and guidelines, with public educational meetings planned to begin in August 2026; first-reading materials cited electric-grid and utility capacity, economic, environmental, and community effects.

properties.date_enacted: June 1, 2026 (County Council third reading and public hearing, adopting Ordinance 25-26-23)
properties.duration: Until January 1, 2028, or until the county adopts regulations for data center/data processing/cryptocurrency mining uses, whichever occurs first
properties.trigger: Immediately stops acceptance, review, or action on zoning approvals, construction permits, site plans, and other county approvals for data centers, data processing facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and related uses in unincorporated Chesterfield County; followed an emergency moratorium adopted April 6, 2026.

properties.date_enacted: September 14, 2026 (County Council third and final reading and public hearing, per WIS; second reading was at an Aug. 24, 2026 special called meeting, first reading Aug. 10, 2026)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: County's Unified Development Code does not specifically define data centers or battery energy storage systems; council sought to close a loophole after learning of a proposed "Project 59" data center in the county industrial park, and to give time to set standards for setbacks, buffers, noise, lighting, and emergency access.

properties.date_enacted: July 6, 2026 (County Council third reading and enactment of Ordinance 26-O-04, effective immediately)
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Pauses consideration of special exceptions, conditional uses, and other land-use approvals for data centers while county staff and the Planning Commission study appropriate locations/conditions and prepare comprehensive-plan and code amendments; also holds received-but-unconsidered applications in abeyance.

properties.date_enacted: September 14, 2026 (County Council final vote approving Ordinance 856, per WLTX; first reading was at a July 20, 2026 special called meeting)
properties.duration: Twelve months
properties.trigger: Inquiries regarding data center development; county lacks a regulatory framework or zoning ordinance structure sufficient to manage the industry's scale and impact.

properties.date_enacted: July 21, 2026 (County Council 4-3 approval of third and final reading of Ordinance 2026-25)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Pause on new data center approvals following citizen concerns; sponsored by Councilmembers Mark Allison, Cathy Miller, and Dayne Pruitt; twenty-four people registered for public comment on third reading.

properties.date_enacted: On or about September 22, 2026 (County Council third and final reading, per WIS reporting published Sept. 23, 2026; first and second readings passed Aug. 25 and Sept. 8, 2026, respectively)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Growing public interest and discussion about the potential impact of data centers on the community; residents raised AI/technology growth concerns during the public hearing.

properties.date_enacted: September 14, 2026 (County Council third and final reading, 6-0 vote, per Fox Carolina/WYFF4)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: County is unzoned; council wants time for public input, planning, and expert testimony before deciding how and where data centers should be regulated.

properties.date_enacted: An initial pause was put in effect around 2026-06-02/06-03 following resident concerns (WIS News 10, 2026-06-03) and the council's rejection of a data center deal (WLTX, 2026-06-07); WRDW reported the county 'passes 1-year data center moratorium' on 2026-06-05. The council then 'unanimously confirmed' the year-long moratorium on 2026-07-16 (WIS News 10; FOX Carolina).
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Resident opposition to a proposed AI data center development and the council's rejection of an associated data center deal

properties.date_enacted: September 8, 2026 (County Council third reading and public hearing, per the county's own official Sept. 8, 2026 agenda; first reading was at a July 23, 2026 special called meeting)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Concerns over data center impacts on residents raised at town halls in July/August 2026; county sought time to study and develop rules before further data center development.

properties.date_enacted: September 21, 2026 (County Council third and final reading, 5-1 vote, per Post and Courier and Fox Carolina; first reading occurred in late June 2026)
properties.duration: One year (12 months)
properties.trigger: Public outcry over power grid strain, water resources, and air quality; moratorium was first proposed in response to the Lightstone Group's proposed data center on Jones Road (a 60-megawatt facility on a former industrial site).

properties.date_enacted: An emergency 60-day moratorium (Ordinance 26-1049) covering solar, BESS, and data centers was approved and took effect immediately at the June 23, 2026 County Council meeting. Companion 180-day moratorium ordinances tailored to each use (Solar: Ordinance 26-1050; BESS: Ordinance 26-1051; Data Centers: Ordinance 26-1052) received second reading, with no public hearing held, at a July 21, 2026 special called meeting. No source reviewed confirmed a third-reading/final-adoption date for 26-1050/1051/1052.
properties.duration: 60 days (Ordinance 26-1049, emergency, effective immediately June 23, 2026); a further 180 days is proposed for each of the three companion ordinances (26-1050 solar, 26-1051 BESS, 26-1052 data centers) but final adoption was not confirmed
properties.trigger: County has no zoning provisions for battery energy storage systems or data centers; follows public opposition to, and council's rejection of, a proposed 1,700-acre solar farm.

properties.date_enacted: July 13, 2026 (County Council third reading and public hearing, effective immediately in unincorporated York County)
properties.duration: Nine months
properties.trigger: Restricts special-exception and conditional-use approvals, site-plan acceptance, and other land-use/development approvals for data centers in unincorporated York County while the county studies utility, water, noise, pollution, infrastructure, and nearby-property impacts.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-20 (City Council first reading and passage, 7-0)
properties.duration: From adoption (immediate effect) through a fixed sunset of November 18, 2026, or the effective date of a zoning ordinance amendment addressing data centers, whichever occurs first
properties.trigger: City's current zoning/building regulations and staff may not adequately address data centers; council found officials 'hampered' in assessing permit applications, creating unpredictability and risk of stranded investment pending a comprehensive study

properties.date_enacted: 2024-11-19 (Board of Commissioners unanimous vote); effective 2024-12-12; extended one additional year by unanimous vote on 2025-10-21

properties.duration: Originally reported as a one-year moratorium on wind energy projects; county Board of Adjustment minutes from September and October 2025 describe a 'Moratorium on Solar and Wind Energy Systems' ordinance adopted by the County Commission, and a public-notice aggregator (not independently verified against an archived primary source) indicated a hearing was set for 2026-08-25 to consider extending a 'temporary moratorium on utility-scale alternative energy systems' county-wide.
properties.trigger: Proposed Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources; up to 97 GE turbines, approximately 248 MW) spanning Turner and Yankton counties; county sought time to study and regulate before the project could proceed

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21 (County Commission adopted the moratorium 5-0, recorded as Action 26248C)

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-27, Austin County Commissioners Court, unanimous vote at a Monday meeting (KWHI, published Tuesday 2026-07-28, reports the vote as taken 'Monday'), following the July 13, 2026 public hearing. The signed order itself (obtained directly from austincounty.com) confirms adoption by the full Commissioners Court (County Judge Tim Lapham and Commissioners Greg Mikel, Bobby Rinn, Leroy Cerny, and Chip Reed) but its scanned signature-page 'Date of adoption' field was not legibly OCR-able.
properties.duration: Until a comprehensive health and safety review is complete, per the posted draft order; no fixed term confirmed
properties.trigger: Comprehensive health and safety review of AI data centers and battery energy storage systems

properties.date_enacted: Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23. City Council gave staff direction on a Tuesday (per dentonrc.com, a 4-3 vote) to proceed with a possible moratorium and stricter development-code amendments; held the first of two required public hearings on 2026-09-22 (no vote taken); a second public hearing is scheduled for 2026-10-27, with final Council consideration possible as early as 2026-12-02.
properties.duration: Proposed 3 months (per Councilmember Suzi Rumohr's public statement)
properties.trigger: grid_energy/infrastructure_capacity: Denton Municipal Electric's transmission system is reported to be operating near capacity, with roughly $300 million in proposed transmission upgrades awaiting an ERCOT response; residents also cited water and community-benefit concerns relative to the roughly $3.5 million in taxes and $9 million in electric ROI/franchise fees existing data centers generate.

properties.date_enacted: Not yet adopted as of 2026-09-23. On 2026-08-11 the City Council voted (nearly unanimous, with one abstention/one dissent on related items) to begin the legal process toward a 90-day data center moratorium, alongside creating an 11-member Data Center & Infrastructure Commission (chaired by TCU professor Michael Slattery) and requiring state regulatory approval (per Gov. Abbott's directive) before city permits. Per the timeline city staff presented, two public hearings on the moratorium and two additional ordinance-reading hearings are still required; a Data Center & Infrastructure Commission report is due at a Nov. 3, 2026 work session.
properties.duration: Proposed 90 days, extendable once by an additional 90 days (to a 180-day maximum); per the city's own timeline as of August 2026, the moratorium itself would not take effect until approximately Feb. 16, 2027 (running to approximately May 17, 2027, extendable to Aug. 15, 2027), after which state law bars the city from imposing another moratorium for two years.
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap and specific_project concerns: sustained public pushback over multiple proposed/under-construction data centers within city limits and the ETJ (e.g., a $10 billion project within 300 feet of a resident's historic garden), a Fort Worth Zoning Commission vote against recommending an initial package of data center zoning regulations (July 2026) as rushed, and a directive from five Council members calling for a moratorium.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-20 (Wednesday commission meeting; ValleyCentral's own article, posted 2026-05-21 at 10:43 a.m., states the vote occurred 'During a Wednesday meeting'; May 20, 2026 was a Wednesday). Subsequently extended by an additional 60 days: first reading of the extension ordinance occurred in the commission meeting reported by KRGV on 2026-08-25 ('approved last week'), with a second/final reading approximately two weeks later (late August 2026).
properties.duration: Initial 120 days from 2026-05-20; City Attorney Mark Sossi described the subsequent 60-day extension (first reading reported ~2026-08-13, second/final reading ~2 weeks later) as 'the maximum extension allowed by law,' bringing the total pause to 180 days. Multiple August 2026 reports describe the extended pause as running 'through December' 2026.
properties.trigger: Precautionary study of potential future data center impacts and modernization of land use regulations; one source (Rio Grande Guardian) noted no data center projects were formally proposed within city limits at the time

properties.date_enacted: 2026-05-12 (Hill County Commissioners Court approved a 1-year moratorium on data center construction, per KWTX)
properties.duration: One year (as adopted; rescinded before completing its term)
properties.trigger: Development pressure from multiple (reportedly up to eight) proposed data center projects in a rural North Texas county

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-23, Lubbock City Council, 5-2 vote (District 6 Councilman Tim Collins and District 4 Councilman Tim Green dissenting), adopting a resolution to begin the process toward a possible 90-day moratorium.
properties.duration: Proposed 90 days, with a possible optional 90-day extension (would push consideration of a large-scale data center to June 2027 if extended); an 18-month moratorium originally proposed by the citizen 'Save Lubbock' group was deemed not feasible under Texas law.
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap and specific_project concerns, driven by a citizen petition ('Save Lubbock' group led by Stephen Sanders); Council members cited ERCOT grid conditions and a desire to await further state-level guidance/regulation before large-scale data center development proceeds.

properties.date_enacted: County Commission unanimously adopted Ordinance 654 on 2026-06-10.
properties.duration: 180-day temporary land-use regulation on data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure in areas where the county retains land-use authority. Stops new land-use and business-license applications, building permits, administrative appeals, conditional use permits, subdivisions, zone changes, site plans, development agreements, and similar approvals. Applications formally determined complete before the effective date may proceed; incomplete covered applications are suspended.
properties.trigger: Adopted while the county develops updated data center regulations, in areas outside the Military Installation Development Authority's Stratos project area.

properties.date_enacted: County Council suspended its rules and voted 6-0 (one member absent) to adopt Ordinance 2026-32 on 2026-06-23.
properties.duration: Proactive 180-day moratorium on data centers and data center power plants across all zones in unincorporated Cache County, pausing covered land-use, license, permit, appeal, conditional-use, subdivision, zone-change, site-plan, development-agreement, and similar applications (applications already determined complete may continue). Directs staff and the Planning Commission to prepare permanent regulations within 150 days.
properties.trigger: Proactive measure; minutes state the county had received no data center inquiries and the action was not a response to a pending project.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-08, Clearfield City Council regular meeting, 4-0 vote (Councilmember Danielle King absent).
properties.duration: 180 days from adoption (to approximately 2027-03-07).
properties.trigger: regulatory_gap; a pending zoning-determination request for a proposed data center in the Freeport Center's M-1 Manufacturing Zone (Building J8) exposed that Clearfield's code has no definition or zoning classification for 'data center,' prompting the Council to pause while it studies electrical demand, water consumption, noise, and other impacts and considers pending state legislation.

properties.date_enacted: County Commission voted 7-0 on 2026-07-07 to adopt a temporary land use regulation, effective immediately.
properties.duration: 180-day pause on acceptance and processing of applications for data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure. Planning and Zoning Director Andrew Jackson said no data center application was pending and the county code lacked a data center definition and standards addressing water, power, noise, lighting, and visual impacts.
properties.trigger: County code lacked a data center definition and standards addressing water, power, noise, lighting, and visual impacts; no data center application was pending.

properties.date_enacted: County Commission approved Ordinance 2026-13 by a 2-0 vote (Commissioner Paul Cozzens absent) on 2026-05-26.
properties.duration: 180 days. Bars acceptance or processing of new applications for data centers, data center power plants, and solar power plants while the county develops updated regulations. Complete applications were exempt (the Pronghorn/Antelope Data Center application was identified as complete and exempt); incomplete pending applications were suspended (the BrightNight Red Butte application was placed on hold).
properties.trigger: Adopted while the county develops updated data center and solar power plant regulations.

properties.date_enacted: Municipal Council voted 5-0 to adopt Ordinance 26-12 on 2026-06-30, following a public hearing; published and effective 2026-07-01.
properties.duration: 180-day moratorium throughout Logan City: the city may not accept, process, approve, or issue an application, permit, or approval authorizing construction or development of a data center or data center power plant, and no person may begin such development. Expires after 180 days unless the council ends it earlier.
properties.trigger: City departments had begun work on land-development and utility-related proposals; adopted to allow further Planning Commission review and public comment.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-04, Sanpete County Commission regular meeting, following a recommendation from the Sanpete County Planning Commission.
properties.duration: Six months from adoption (to approximately 2027-01-31); county officials described the moratorium as renewable 'six months at a time' as long as the county shows it is working toward permanent regulations.
properties.trigger: County code contains no ordinance governing data centers; commissioners wanted time to draft and adopt land-use standards before any development proposal could be submitted under existing (silent) county code.

properties.date_enacted: County Commission voted 3-0 to approve Resolution 2026-04 on 2026-07-08.
properties.duration: 180-day temporary suspension on land use applications for data centers and data center power plants, applying throughout zoned and unzoned unincorporated Wayne County. Covers land use and business-license applications, building permits, administrative appeals, conditional use permits, subdivisions, zone changes, site plans, development agreements, and related approvals.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-31 (Select Board and Village Board of Trustees joint unanimous vote, dated interim zoning bylaw)
properties.duration: Two years from adoption, as an interim zoning bylaw
properties.trigger: Town bylaws are silent on data centers and 'high-impact uses'; board wants time for the planning commission to study electric-grid, water, noise, and hazardous-waste impacts before any application is filed, prompted in part by community reaction to a separate large industrial-park/quarry proposal

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-21 (City Council adopted Resolution 26-R-042 by a 9-0 vote)
properties.duration: 8 months from adoption, or until City Council takes final action on comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever occurs first

Data centers were by-right uses in I-1 and I-2 districts, and the Board directed staff to prepare amendments requiring special use permits.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-06, Front Royal Town Council work session, 6-0 vote (Vice Mayor Amber F. Veitenthal and Councilmembers DeDomenico-Payne, Ingram, Rappaport, Sealock, and Wood; Mayor Cockrell present but votes only to break ties), per the town's own approved council minutes.
properties.duration: 90 days from adoption (to approximately 2026-10-04).
properties.trigger: The town sought to preserve the status quo while it drafts a permanent zoning text amendment to define data centers separately from 'technology' uses and prohibit data centers in all town zoning districts; no data center application had been received as of adoption.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-09-16, Loudoun County Board of Supervisors, 7-1-1 vote (Supervisor opposed on the base pause; a separate 7-1-1 vote with Supervisor Briskman opposed approved a grid-reliability substation exception), per the Board's own press release.
properties.duration: Open-ended; in effect while the Board continues Phase 2 of its Data Center Standards and Locations initiative (zoning ordinance and comprehensive plan amendments), which is anticipated to be completed in 2027. County staff are to return with a formal resolution memorializing the pause at the Board's October 20, 2026 Business Meeting.
properties.trigger: Regulatory gap and community pressure over rapid data center growth in the county ("Data Center Alley"); effort led by Algonkian District Supervisor Juli Briskman, tied to the county's ongoing Phase 2 Data Center Standards and Locations initiative (begun September 2025) addressing data center/substation siting, noise, building heights, on-site power generation, and battery storage standards.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-18, Virginia Beach City Council, unanimous vote.
properties.duration: 12 months from adoption, or until City Council takes final action on an ordinance regulating data centers, whichever occurs first (to approximately 2027-08-18).
properties.trigger: City zoning ordinance does not specifically define or regulate data centers; concerns raised over resource consumption (water, electricity), noise, and land-use compatibility, following an informal June 2026 Council statement opposing large-scale/hyperscale data centers.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-03-03 (interim zoning controls prohibiting BESS citywide, Ordinance No. 26-1246, superseding an earlier BESS permit-application moratorium first adopted 2024-02-15 under Ordinance No. 24-1205 and renewed by Ordinance No. 25-1219 in February 2025); extended a further six months, with a small-system exception, by Ordinance No. 26-1258 (public hearing scheduled 2026-10-06)

properties.date_enacted: City Council adopted Ordinance 905 by a 6-0 vote on 2026-06-29, effective immediately.
properties.duration: One-year moratorium in all city districts on accepting, processing, or approving applications to establish, expand, or change a use to a data center with capacity exceeding 20 MVA. Preserves vested rights for complete permit applications filed before the effective date. Public hearing scheduled for 2026-07-13.
12 months from passage; automatically expired April 2019 unless extended (Ordinance 2018-1538, Section 3)

properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Chelan County PUD briefings on high-density-load growth, limited electrical capacity, and fire-safety risk in areas not designed for such loads

properties.date_enacted: 2018-05 (Columbia Basin Herald reported on 2018-05-28 that Moses Lake "City Council has passed an ordinance" "last week" that prohibits new operations; consistent with a May 2018 enactment date)
properties.duration: Up to 12 months (per Columbia Basin Herald: "for up to 12 months and will give the city time to study the impacts")
properties.trigger: City received inquiries for cryptocurrency operations; local report cited seven known operations (four unpermitted), a recent fire tied to an unpermitted Central Business District operation, residential-zone complaints, and absence of zoning-code treatment

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-09 (Seattle City Council unanimous final passage of Council Bill 121214 and companion Resolution 32204, under emergency designation); signed by Mayor Katie Wilson 2026-06-11; Ordinance No. 127447

properties.duration: Initial six-month interim official control under RCW 35A.63.220 and RCW 36.70A.390; extended for an additional six months by Ordinance 2019-04 (effective approximately 2019-02-23) until permanent zoning amendments were adopted
properties.trigger: Cryptocurrency mining/high-density-load growth, power-distribution concerns, and fire/safety concerns identified during the Chelan PUD-driven regional response

properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Blue Fern Development's July 28, 2026 proposal for a roughly 100,000-sq-ft, 20 MW 'research sized' data center within a residential/commercial development near I-90; concerns over electricity, water, fire protection, noise, and local economic effects

properties.date_enacted: 2024-05-14 (original 12-month BESS moratorium, Ordinance No. 07-2024); renewed six months at a time by Ordinance No. 03-2025, No. 09-2025, and most recently No. 02-2026 (adopted 2026-04-14)
properties.duration: Initial 12 months, renewed in successive six-month increments; the current renewal (Ordinance No. 02-2026) was adopted 2026-04-14 concurrently with a public hearing
properties.trigger: BESS facilities present fire, explosion, hazardous-chemical, noise, visual, and wildlife-impact risks not addressed by the City's outdated 'Utility Facility' zoning definition (CMC 18.20.050/18.125.040); City wants to align with King County's BESS siting standards and Dept. of Ecology guidance before permitting such facilities

properties.date_enacted: 2018-04-17, Board of Douglas County Commissioners approved a moratorium on the use of cargo containers to house cryptocurrency mining operations in unincorporated Douglas County (per Wenatchee World, published 2018-04-17, describing the vote as taken 'Tuesday')
properties.duration: Not verified from primary ordinance text; MRSC characterizes the action as a moratorium on cargo-container cryptocurrency mining operations
properties.trigger: The Board's primary stated concern was the aesthetics of cargo containers used to house cryptocurrency mining equipment in unincorporated areas (cargo containers were otherwise broadly allowed countywide, with only the East Wenatchee Urban Growth Area separately regulating their placement and appearance). Separately, Douglas County PUD had issued its own 3-month moratorium on electric service applications for cryptocurrency/data-mining loads, running March-May 2014 (not 2018), later replaced by a tiered rate structure and contract requirements for consumers using 1.5+ MW.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-06-02, City Council unanimous vote adopting Ordinance No. 1353 (signed 2026-06-03)
properties.duration: The ordinance's title recites a six-month term, but its recitals/findings state the Council 'deems it necessary...to impose a moratorium...for a period of 12 months'; the operative duration section was not fully captured in the text retrieved this pass

properties.duration: Originally 12 months; an extension was under council consideration as the original term neared its ~2026-02-24 expiration
properties.trigger: Concern over a BESS proposed in a residential neighborhood near Matson Middle School in unincorporated King County (which Covington's City Council formally opposed in a letter); fire, health, and environmental risk concerns raised by residents

properties.date_enacted: City Council unanimously adopted emergency Ordinance No. 26-1048 on 2026-07-07, effective immediately.
properties.duration: 12-month citywide moratorium barring the siting, creation, or expansion of data centers and the acceptance, processing, or approval of related land-use and building-permit applications, for facilities exceeding 1 megawatt or 4,000 square feet. Preserves vested rights. Public hearing scheduled for 2026-09-01.

properties.date_enacted: 2025-06-11 (original 365-day BESS moratorium, Ordinance No. 639-2025); extended 180 days by Ordinance No. 645-2026 following a 2026-05-11 public hearing
properties.duration: 365 days initially, plus a 180-day extension
properties.trigger: Increased developer requests to site BESS facilities countywide; County zoning code does not contemplate BESS development or ensure adequate protections; County wants to complete workplan studies (fire, noise, wildlife, Dept. of Ecology guidance, HB 1216/WAC 51.54A.0322 compliance) before adopting permanent regulations

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-10, Board of County Commissioners approved (2-0, one commissioner absent) an emergency six-month moratorium on data center applications by resolution; extended a further six months following a 2026-09-15 public hearing
properties.duration: Originally six months; extended an additional six months on/around 2026-09-15 (approximately one year total)
properties.trigger: Concerns stemming from Cle Elum-area (Blue Fern Development) interest in siting a data center in Upper Kittitas County; county code does not adequately define or classify data centers for land use, zoning, environmental, building, infrastructure, and permitting review

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-28, Town Council unanimous vote adopting an emergency moratorium (likely Ordinance No. 1274, per the ordinance-number tracker shown on the July 28, 2026 council agenda; the draft ordinance text itself left the number blank)
properties.duration: Six months minimum; by its own terms the moratorium does not terminate until the Council, following the required public hearing, adopts findings and either extends or cancels it -- termination is not presumed to occur merely because six months have elapsed
properties.trigger: Town lacks guidelines/policies addressing data centers' large-scale water and electricity use, which could strain public infrastructure, deplete water resources during drought, and constrain industrial growth/climate resilience; adopted following Skagit County's June 2026 moratorium

properties.date_enacted: City Council unanimously adopted Ordinance No. 3381 on 2026-07-13.
properties.duration: Six-month pause on acceptance, processing, and approval of land-use and permit applications for facilities whose principal use is digital-data processing, storage, management, or transmission; incidental server equipment supporting another principal use is excluded. Public hearing required within 60 days.
properties.trigger: Study period covers siting, public safety, land-use compatibility, water and sewer planning, utility rates, and permanent code amendments.

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-12, City Council vote (one dissent) for a six-month moratorium, Ordinance No. 3943
properties.duration: Six months
properties.trigger: Concerns over electricity and water demand, city capacity to accommodate large facilities, stormwater/sewer planning, and the city's location within the Skagit River 100-year floodplain

properties.date_enacted: 2025-05-28 (original BESS moratorium, Ordinance No. 3913); continued/ratified by Ordinance No. 3915 (adopted 2025-07-23) for a maximum of one year from Ordinance 3913's adoption
properties.duration: Maximum one year from adoption of Ordinance 3913 (2025-05-28), i.e., through approximately 2026-05-28, unless terminated earlier or further renewed after another public hearing
properties.trigger: City lacked siting criteria/safety standards/emergency-response requirements for grid-scale BESS; concern over lithium-ion fire and thermal-runaway risk, noise, and aesthetic compatibility with residential/retail zones

properties.date_enacted: 2026-07-20, City Council unanimously (6-0) adopted emergency Ordinance No. 4850

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-25, County Council passed Emergency Ordinance No. 2026-557 by a 6-1 vote (Councilmember Dave Morell dissenting)

properties.date_enacted: 2026-08-18, Board of Commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-22 (unanimous), after first approving it by motion earlier in the same meeting

properties.trigger: Eight of nine public commenters at the August 18, 2026 meeting requested a pause on data center development, citing electricity/water demand, noise/light, limited county land and resources, and the view that applications 'seem to pop out of nowhere at a rapid pace'; no specific project or pending applications

properties.date_enacted: County Council approved Emergency Ordinance 26-026 on 2026-06-24, effective immediately.

Requires a public hearing within 60 days and permits six-month renewals after hearing and findings.
