properties.date_enacted: June 16, 2026 (Common Council unanimous adoption of Resolution R26-13876)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Pause on accepting, processing, approving, or issuing permits, licenses, zoning approvals, conditional-use permits, site plans, or other development approvals for new data centers; matter referred to Plan Commission for study.

properties.date_enacted: Introduced 2026-05-26; approved by the County Board 2026-06-04; signed by County Executive Melissa Agard on/around 2026-06-09
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: Mounting hyperscale data-center development pressure near Madison; the county formed a 13-member Advisory Committee on Data Centers (ACDC) in parallel to study impacts

properties.date_enacted: August 18, 2026 (County Board of Supervisors, 29-2 vote, following an Aug. 10, 2026 Land and Resources and Parks Committee public hearing and unanimous committee approval)
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: Concerns about groundwater and environmental impacts from a Meta data center under construction in Beaver Dam (within the county); supervisor Cathy Houchin sought an impact study alongside the moratorium.

properties.date_enacted: May 26, 2026 (Door County Board of Supervisors adoption of Resolution 2026-41 by voice vote, per the board's own official meeting minutes). properties.duration: Up to 12 months
properties.trigger: Pause on development of data centers and battery energy storage systems in unincorporated Door County to allow investigation, planning, and regulation of potential impacts; Board may extend by separate action.

properties.date_enacted: June 16, 2026 (County Board adoption of Resolution 2026-14)
properties.duration: Up to 12 months
properties.trigger: Pause on accepting applications for, or granting zoning-related permits for, hyperscale data centers (at least 5,000 servers and at least 10,000 sq ft) in unincorporated areas under county zoning.

properties.date_enacted: July 14, 2026 (County Board adoption of Ordinance 26-0703, one member opposed)

properties.trigger: Stops acceptance of data center applications in county-zoned territory while the county studies impacts, receives local input, and develops consistent standards.

properties.date_enacted: July 13, 2026 (Village Board approval, 5-0 vote)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Plan Commission and Village Board wanted to get ahead of potential data center proposals and avoid being "surprised"; part of a wave of similar actions among nearby Fox Valley/Northeast Wisconsin municipalities.

properties.date_enacted: August 13, 2026 (Common Council unanimous final vote, following City Plan Commission advancement August 3, 2026 and a Judiciary & Administration Committee public hearing August 5, 2026)
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: City is following La Crosse County's lead (the county adopted its own 18-month moratorium in June 2026); city lacks zoning language addressing data centers and wants time to study environmental, economic, and health impacts alongside the county's ad hoc study committee.

properties.date_enacted: June 18, 2026 (County Board approval, 26-2 vote, per WIZM)
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: Adopted to give the county time to receive the Data Center Study Committee's work (first met June 10, 2026) and consider permanent rules.

properties.duration: 18 months from the date the ordinance is published (its effective date), or until the County Board adopts and the County Executive approves amendments, or rescinds the moratorium, whichever occurs first
properties.trigger: Town petitions from Mishicot, Two Creeks, and Two Rivers; concerns about health and safety, air quality, water resources, water use, electricity demand, fire hazards, public services, roads, property values, noise, visual impacts, farmland preservation, and lack of county data center standards.

properties.date_enacted: August 25, 2026 (County Board approval)
properties.duration: At least 12 months
properties.trigger: High electrical demand, utility infrastructure requirements, cooling/mechanical systems, noise, emergency power generation, and land-use compatibility concerns associated with data center development; 7 of 18 affected townships responded to a staff survey in support before passage.

properties.duration: Proposed one year
properties.trigger: Milwaukee's zoning code does not currently treat data centers as a distinct land use; sponsor wants rules in place before a major data center proposal is submitted, following controversy over a since-withdrawn data center component of a Midtown Center Walmart-site redevelopment.

properties.date_enacted: July 21, 2026 (County Board 10-3 adoption of Resolution 07-26-04, three supervisors absent)
properties.duration: Up to 18 months
properties.trigger: Stops receipt of applications and issuance of zoning-related permits for medium and large data centers and battery storage facilities.

properties.date_enacted: August 18, 2026 (County Board unanimous voice vote)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: County has no existing ordinance addressing data centers; board wants time to educate itself and draft rules before any proposal arrives; no known data center plans exist in the county currently.

properties.date_enacted: September 8, 2026 (Common Council unanimous vote)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: City wants time to study data centers and develop informed, consistent zoning and regulatory standards; part of a coordinated Fox Valley effort with Winnebago County and the East Central Wisconsin Regional Planning Commission.

properties.date_enacted: September 15, 2026 (County Board approval, 27-1 vote)
properties.duration: 18 months
properties.trigger: County has no specific zoning mechanism for data centers; officials want time to research the industry and draft zoning guardrails before any project comes forward; explicitly applies only in areas under county zoning authority.

properties.date_enacted: June 24, 2026 (County Board adoption, following a June 3, 2026 public hearing)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Pause on siting, construction, establishment, or expansion of data centers in unincorporated towns using county zoning; pending requests held in abeyance, existing valid approvals exempt.

properties.date_enacted: September 1, 2026 (County Board of Supervisors approval, 18-0 vote)

properties.trigger: Public concern following a smaller data center (Metered Mining) receiving a conditional use permit in the Village of Hammond and subsequent litigation; county currently defines large-scale data centers as those demanding 10 megawatts or more but lacks a comprehensive regulatory framework.

properties.date_enacted: September 15, 2026 (Village Board, following a public hearing that drew more than 70 residents)

properties.trigger: At least one developer inquiry (Blake Simpson) about a proposed data center in the village; officials wanted time to establish zoning policies before any application; Shawano County's own June 2026 moratorium does not cover Tigerton because the village has its own zoning.

properties.trigger: Pause on placing data centers in the town while the Plan Commission and Zoning Administrator research and develop siting, zoning, and operating rules.

properties.duration: Proposed 12 months
properties.trigger: County currently lacks local zoning regulations for data centers, battery energy storage systems, or large-scale solar; officials cite fire hazards (BESS), noise/vibration from cooling units, light pollution, water/air quality, stormwater runoff, and traffic impacts.

properties.date_enacted: June 23, 2026 (Village Board adoption of Ordinance O6-1-26, following a June 2, 2026 Plan Commission recommendation)

properties.trigger: Pause on receiving applications and granting permits/approvals for hyperscale data centers, defined as facilities with at least 100,000 sq ft floor area or at least 20 MW planned or installed electrical capacity.

properties.date_enacted: July 20, 2026 (Village Board adoption of Ordinance 13-2026)
properties.duration: 12 months, or until a regulating ordinance is approved or finally rejected, whichever occurs first
properties.trigger: Bars new applications/permits for principal-use data centers larger than 10,000 sq ft; accessory data centers and complete applications filed before the effective date are excepted.

properties.date_enacted: July 7, 2026 (Village Board 4-1 approval of Ordinance 2026-07)
properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Pause on data center development to allow the village to draft regulatory rules and standards.

properties.duration: One year
properties.trigger: Adopted following a resident petition, while an August 11, 2026 advisory referendum on municipal utility/infrastructure commitments for a large-scale data center project remained scheduled.

properties.date_enacted: April 6, 2026 (Town Board regular meeting)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: Modeled on a similar moratorium passed by the City of Madison; adopted amid growing data center prospecting activity in Dane County.

properties.date_enacted: August 18, 2026 (County Board voice vote, one dissenting supervisor)
properties.duration: 12 months
properties.trigger: No county mechanism to regulate data centers; concerns over energy/water use, noise pollution, and utility rate impacts amid a wave of similar Wisconsin county and city moratoria.
